  • HMAS Stirling (Fleet Base West) - AUKUS SRF-West, Australia military · -32.2417, 115.6833HMAS Stirling on Garden Island off Rockingham is the Royal Australian Navy's submarine home port and the designated site for AUKUS 'Submarine Rotational Force – West': from 2027 up to four US and one UK nuclear-powered submarines will rotate through, backed by an Australian investment of up to A$8 billion. Disclosed assets of at least $806M (Jan 2025).
  • Hunneschans (Duno ring-fort), Heveadorp governance · 1000 · 51.9715, 5.8109Rijksmonument 45966: early-medieval fortification with earthen rampart and moat (Carolingian, c.1000 AD) on the Duno hill at Heveadorp, Renkum municipality.   • Obelisk of Montevideo (a los Constituyentes de 1830), Uruguay obelisk · 1938 · -34.8974, -56.1644A 40 m three-sided pink-granite obelisk by sculptor Jose Luis Zorrilla de San Martin, inaugurated 1938 at the entrance to Parque Batlle, bearing three bronze figures for 'Law', 'Liberty' and 'Force' to honor the framers of Uruguay's first 1830 constitution. Source: Wikipedia, 'Obelisk of Montevideo'.
  • Obelisk of Senusret I (Al-Masalla), Heliopolis, Cairo obelisk · 30.1293, 31.3075The 20.7 m, roughly 120-ton red-granite obelisk raised by Pharaoh Senusret I around 1940 BC is the oldest standing obelisk in Egypt and the sole surviving element of the great Temple of Ra-Atum at ancient Heliopolis, now swallowed by Cairo's Matariya district. It marks the ancient priestly-solar power center that gave the West its obelisk form. Source: Wikipedia, 'Al-Masalla' / EgyptToday, 'Meet the Obelisk of Senusret I'.
  • Obelisk of Theodosius, Istanbul (Hippodrome) obelisk · 390 · 41.0063, 28.9752Upper part of an obelisk of Thutmose III (1479-1425 BC) from Karnak; originally ~30 m, now 18.54 m (25.6 m with base) - the lower part was damaged in antiquity. Constantius II had it taken to Alexandria (357); Theodosius I set it up on the Hippodrome spina in 390. Its marble base shows Theodosius with captives. Egyptian, Roman, Byzantine, Ottoman: it stayed where Theodosius put it.
  • Offutt AFB - U.S. Strategic Command (STRATCOM) HQ, Nebraska military · 1948 · 41.1172, -95.9082Offutt AFB near Omaha — home of Strategic Air Command from 1948 — is headquarters of U.S. Strategic Command, responsible for the nation's nuclear deterrent, global strike and nuclear command-and-control. A new $1.3 billion command-and-control facility, the Gen. Curtis E. LeMay Building, was dedicated there in 2019. Source: Wikipedia, 'United States Strategic Command'; Military Times; GlobalSecurity.org.
  • Open Society Foundations HQ - New York governance · 1993 · 40.7659, -73.9815George Soros's grantmaking network, founded in 1993, is headquartered at 224 West 57th Street in Manhattan. With an endowment of roughly $23 billion, it funds civil-society, human-rights and media groups worldwide and is a recurring target of political campaigns internationally. Source: Open Society Foundations — Wikipedia / GuideStar.
  • Osan Air Base, South Korea military · 37.0908, 127.030051st Fighter Wing and Seventh Air Force HQ, near Pyeongtaek, 40 miles south of Seoul and about 60 miles from the DMZ.
  • Pantheon Obelisk (Macuteo Obelisk), Piazza della Rotonda, Rome obelisk · 1711 · 41.8993, 12.4769A 6.34 m Egyptian obelisk bearing Ramesses II's cartouches, from Heliopolis, later in Domitian's sanctuary of Isis; excavated in the 14th or 16th century and set on the fountain before the Pantheon by Pope Clement XI in 1711. One of the 13 ancient obelisks in Rome.
  • Pavlovsk Bay (near Vladivostok) - Pacific Fleet submarine base military · 42.9000, 132.7300Pacific Fleet submarine base near Vladivostok. The Pacific SSBN force - Borei-class boats with Bulava missiles (6 MIRVs each) - is based at Rybachiy, Vilyuchinsk, on Kamchatka.
  • People's Bank of China, Beijing financial · 39.9072, 116.3545The PBOC is the central bank of China, managing the world's largest foreign-exchange reserves (over US$3 trillion) and issuing the renminbi. It pioneered a state-controlled central bank digital currency (the digital yuan / e-CNY) and is a central instrument of China's financial statecraft. Source: Wikipedia, People's Bank of China.
  • Piazza Navona Obelisk (Fountain of Four Rivers), Rome obelisk · 1651 · 41.8990, 12.4729Bernini's Fountain of Four Rivers (1651). Roman-made obelisk (not Egyptian import) - cut in Aswan granite imitating pharaonic style. Bernini: four river gods representing the four known continents. The Nile god's head covered - because the Nile's source was unknown. The obelisk sitting on a void: the power symbol whose origin even its makers didn't fully understand.
  • Pituffik Space Base (formerly Thule Air Base), Greenland military · 1959 · 76.5312, -68.7031Northernmost U.S. base; renamed Pituffik Space Base 6 April 2023. Ballistic-missile early warning and space surveillance. Project Iceworm (1959-67) planned mobile nuclear missile sites under the ice, tested at Camp Century; Denmark never consented and the plan came to light only in 1995.
  • Place Vendôme Column, Paris obelisk · 1810 · 48.8675, 2.3294Not an obelisk but a column (1806-1810) modelled on Trajan's Column for Austerlitz. Its 425 bronze relief plates were said to be cast from captured enemy cannon - the propaganda figure is far above the ~180 guns actually taken at Austerlitz. Torn down by the Paris Commune on 16 May 1871 and rebuilt; Gustave Courbet was billed for reconstruction and died in exile in Switzerland. The column made of enemy weapons, destroyed by revolutionaries, rebuilt by the state.
  • Place de la Concorde Obelisk, Paris obelisk · 48.8656, 2.3212Obelisk of Luxor: one of a pair carved for the portal of Luxor Temple under Ramesses II (c.1250 BC); its twin still stands at Luxor. Not part of the London-New York pair, which came from Heliopolis via Alexandria.
  • Plesetsk Cosmodrome, Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia military · 1957-07-15 · 62.9271, 40.5777More orbital launches than any other site (over 1,500 by 1997). Built from 1957 as an R-7 ICBM base; space launches since 17 March 1966 (military satellites, GLONASS, Angara). The USSR did not admit it existed until 1983. Northernmost spaceport until Andoya (Norway) in 2025-26.
  • Pokhran Test Range - Operation Shakti, Rajasthan, India military · 1998-05-11 · 27.0789, 71.7222At the Pokhran Test Range in the Thar Desert, India conducted the Pokhran-II (Operation Shakti) series of five underground nuclear detonations on 11–13 May 1998, including a claimed 45-kiloton thermonuclear device, moving India to declared nuclear-weapons status and triggering international sanctions. Source: Wikipedia, 'Pokhran-II'; Nuclear Weapon Archive, 'Operation Shakti: 1998'.
  • Psychiatrisch Ziekenhuis Wolfheze (Pro Persona), Netherlands governance · 1944-09-17 · 52.0042, 5.7864Psychiatric hospital founded 1906 on 86 hectares of woodland bought by a Christian care association; merged into De Gelderse Roos (1996), now part of Pro Persona (2009). On 17 Sept 1944, at the opening of Operation Market Garden, English bombers struck the hospital buildings - the Allies suspected German troops there - killing 81; the gliders landed on the nearby Reijerscamp heath. Its 1907 water tower (architect E. Knevel) and other buildings are municipal monuments.
  • Quirinal Obelisk, Piazza del Quirinale, Rome obelisk · 1786 · 41.8993, 12.4865A ~14.6 m ancient Roman obelisk moved from the Mausoleum of Augustus and re-erected in 1786 by Pope Pius VI between the colossal Dioscuri statues, directly before the Quirinal Palace - former papal residence and now the official residence of the President of the Italian Republic. Source: Wikipedia, 'Obelisks of Rome' (Quirinal obelisk).
  • RAF Ascension Island, South Atlantic military · -7.9694, -14.3939Wideawake Airfield - 10,000-ft runway on volcanic island. Critical relay for Falklands War logistics. NASA tracking station. GCHQ/NSA signals intelligence. Shared between military, intelligence, and space agencies on a volcanic rock in the mid-Atlantic.
  • RAF Lakenheath, Suffolk, UK military · 52.4093, 0.560848th Fighter Wing - F-15E and, since 2021, F-35A. 2024 contracts for nuclear-weapons storage facilities; July 2025 flight evidence suggested B61-12 bombs were delivered (unconfirmed by the U.S. or UK).
  • Ramstein Air Base, Germany military · 49.4369, 7.6003HQ USAFE-AFAFRICA. Reported since 2014 (NDR, WDR, Sueddeutsche; Snowden documents) as a satellite relay for U.S. drone operations in Yemen, Somalia and Pakistan; Yemeni families sued Germany over it in 2019. The Kaiserslautern Military Community houses about 54,000 U.S. service members.
  • Ream Naval Base - China-Backed Expansion, Cambodia military · 2023-12 · 10.5058, 103.6133China financed a major upgrade of Cambodia's Ream Naval Base from 2022, adding a 300-metre deepwater pier, a 5,000-ton dry dock and a slipway; two Chinese Type-056A corvettes have been stationed there near-continuously since December 2023, prompting US concern it could become a PLA Navy foothold on the Gulf of Thailand. Source: CSIS Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative; Nikkei Asia; NPR (2025).
  • Rothschild & Co, New Court, London financial · 1919 · 51.5123, -0.0890New Court on St Swithin's Lane has been the London seat of the Rothschild banking house since Nathan Mayer Rothschild established N M Rothschild & Sons there (1809-1811). It hosted the twice-daily London gold fixing from soon after its first sitting (12 Sept 1919) until 2004, when Rothschild withdrew and the fix moved to a telephone call. The firm remains a leading independent M&A adviser.
  • Royal Military Academy Sandhurst, UK military · 51.3484, -0.7693Trained King Abdullah II (Jordan), Sultan Qaboos (Oman) and Crown Prince Hussein of Jordan (2017); King Hamad of Bahrain passed out of Mons Officer Cadet School (1968), later merged into Sandhurst. The empire ended; the officer pipeline did not.
  • SWIFT Headquarters, La Hulpe, Belgium financial · 1973-05-03 · 50.7346, 4.4790SWIFT, the cooperative that runs the dominant global interbank financial-messaging network, links more than 11,000 institutions across over 200 countries and carries tens of millions of messages daily. Control over SWIFT access has become a key instrument of financial sanctions, as when Russian banks were cut off in 2022. Source: Wikipedia, SWIFT (Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication).
  • San Jacinto Monument, La Porte, Texas obelisk · 1936 · 29.7499, -95.0807At 172.92 m (567.31 ft) and topped by a 220-ton Lone Star, this 1936-39 obelisk on the Houston Ship Channel is the world's tallest masonry column, taller than the Washington Monument, commemorating the 1836 Battle of San Jacinto that secured Texan independence. Source: Wikipedia, 'San Jacinto Monument'.
  • Santiago, Chile - 1973 Allende Coup military · 1973-09-11 · -33.4489, -70.669311 Sept 1973: Allende died in La Moneda during the coup. The Church Committee study Covert Action in Chile 1963-1973 documented CIA funding of the opposition (about $8 million, 1970-73; figure attributed). Under Pinochet about 3,000 people were killed or disappeared.
  • Sevastopol, Crimea - Black Sea Fleet military · 2014 · 44.6167, 33.5254Black Sea Fleet base since 1783 and its HQ, with Novorossiysk. Cold War submarine base carved into the mountain at Balaklava. Besieged in the Crimean War (1854-55); annexed by Russia in 2014.
  • Severodvinsk / Sevmash, Arkhangelsk Oblast, Russia military · 64.5635, 39.8302Sevmash - Russia's largest shipyard and today its only nuclear-submarine builder: Borei SSBNs, Yasen SSGNs and Belgorod (Poseidon carrier). Closed city.
  • Severomorsk - Northern Fleet HQ, Russia military · 69.0670, 33.4170Headquarters of the Russian Northern Fleet: nuclear submarine force and surface fleet. Ice-free Kola Gulf (Gulf Stream). Submarine bases at Polyarny, Gadzhiyevo and Vidyayevo nearby; Murmansk is the regional port city.
  • Shaheed Minar (Ochterlony Monument), Kolkata obelisk · 1828 · 22.5629, 88.3493A 48 m column-obelisk built in 1828 to honor East India Company general David Ochterlony, fusing Egyptian, Syrian and Turkish motifs; independent India renamed it Shaheed Minar ('Martyrs' Tower') in 1969, converting a colonial monument into a memorial to freedom fighters. Source: Wikipedia, 'Shaheed Minar, Kolkata' / Maps of India.
  • Sohae Satellite Launching Station - Tongchang-ri, North Korea military · 2022-03 · 39.6600, 124.7050Sohae (Tongchang-ri) on North Korea's northwest coast is the DPRK's primary long-range rocket facility and the site of all seven of its satellite launch attempts since 2012, doubling as a testbed for ICBM development. Following Kim Jong Un's March 2022 visit, satellite imagery has shown near-constant expansion of pads, an assembly building and a new sea port. Source: CSIS Beyond Parallel; 38 North; NTI Facilities Profile.
  • Soto Cano Air Base, Honduras military · 14.3822, -87.6212Joint Task Force-Bravo. U.S. military presence in Central America since Cold War. Same Honduras where ISA ran Operation Queens Hunter. Proximity to School of Americas graduates who governed the region.
  • Souda Bay, Crete, Greece military · 35.4875, 24.1194NATO and Hellenic Navy base; deep, naturally protected harbour whose K-14 quay is the only Mediterranean pier able to berth supercarriers. U.S. munitions and logistics hub for the eastern Mediterranean.
  • State Street HQ, Boston corporate · 42.3628, -71.0586US$4.7 trillion AUM (2024). Third of the 'Big Three' index managers with BlackRock and Vanguard; custodian bank for institutional money. Fichtner, Heemskerk & Garcia-Bernardo (2017, 2015 data): combined, the Big Three were the largest shareholder in 438 of the S&P 500 (88%) and used coordinated voting strategies, generally voting with management except at director elections.
  • Svalbard Global Seed Vault, Arctic Norway underground · 2008-02-26 · 78.2355, 15.4942Opened 26 February 2008. Built, owned and fully funded by the Government of Norway; run by NordGen with the Crop Trust part-funding operations. Seeds are held under 'black box' terms: boxes are never opened and only the depositing genebank can withdraw them. First withdrawal: ICARDA, 2015-2019, to rebuild a collection lost to the Syrian war. 1.4 million+ samples from 134 institutions (2026).
  • Tegucigalpa, Honduras - SEASPRAY/ISA Operations Base military · 1982 · 14.0723, -87.1921Operation Queens Hunter (early 1980s): ISA SIGINT specialists flying in SEASPRAY Beechcraft King Airs based in Honduras monitored Salvadoran guerrilla communications. In the same theatre, SOA-trained officers led death squads (attributed); the report reads this as one government funding both.
  • Tehran, Iran - 1953 Operation Ajax military · 1953-08-19 · 35.6892, 51.389019 Aug 1953: CIA-MI6 operation removed Prime Minister Mohammad Mosaddegh and strengthened the Shah; the U.S. has since officially acknowledged its role. CIA helped establish and train SAVAK (Mossad role attributed). The report reads 1979 as blowback.
  • The Alamo (Astor Place Cube), New York City obelisk · 1967 · 40.7296, -73.9912Tony Rosenthal's 'Alamo' (1967). 8-foot cor-ten steel cube balanced on vertex - rotates when pushed. The spinning cube at the intersection. Cube geometry: Kaaba (Mecca), Black Cube of Saturn symbolism, Borg (Star Trek), 2001: A Space Odyssey monolith. The cube that invites you to spin it. Public art as participatory occult geometry.
  • The Sphere (Koenig), Originally WTC Plaza, Now Liberty Park obelisk · 1971 · 40.7115, -74.0134Fritz Koenig's 'The Sphere' (1971). Originally centered in WTC Austin J. Tobin Plaza - between the Twin Towers. Survived 9/11 damaged but intact. Moved to Battery Park, then Liberty Park (2017). The sculpture that stood between two towers and survived their fall. Originally symbolized 'world peace through world trade.' Now a memorial. The sphere between the towers.
  • Tower of the Juche Idea (Juche Tower), Pyongyang obelisk · 1982 · 39.0176, 125.7637Completed 1982 for Kim Il Sung's 70th birthday, this 170 m granite spire is the tallest granite structure in the world, built from 25,550 blocks (one per day of the leader's first 70 years) and capped by a 20 m illuminated metal torch - a state monument to the ruling Juche ideology. Source: Wikipedia, 'Juche Tower'.
  • Trilateral Commission (founded New York, 1973) governance · 1973-07 · 40.7540, -73.9723Founded July 1973 by David Rockefeller and Zbigniew Brzezinski. Published The Crisis of Democracy (1975; Crozier, Huntington, Watanuki) on the governability of democracies. North American Group now based in Washington D.C.
  • Ugland House, George Town, Cayman Islands financial · 19.2920, -81.3854This five-story building, home to the law firm Maples and Calder, is the registered office for roughly 40,000 companies — a density that prompted President Obama to call it 'either the biggest building or the biggest tax scam on record.' It is an icon of offshore corporate structuring. Source: Wikipedia, Ugland House; Foreign Policy, 'House of 19,000 Corporations'.
  • Vanguard HQ, Malvern, Pennsylvania corporate · 40.0430, -75.5146US$13.3 trillion AUM (2025). Largest provider of mutual funds; second-largest ETF provider after BlackRock's iShares. Vanguard is owned by the funds it manages, and so by their investors - it has no outside shareholders. With BlackRock and State Street it is one of the 'Big Three' index managers.
  • Vatican City - St. Peter's Square obelisk · 1929-02-11 · 41.9022, 12.4539Independent city-state since the Lateran Treaty, 11 Feb 1929; elective absolute monarchy; seat of a church of about 1.3 billion baptised Catholics. The obelisk came from Heliopolis (per Pliny) via Alexandria; Caligula shipped it to Rome c. 40 AD.
  • Vessel (Hudson Yards), New York City obelisk · 2019 · 40.7532, -74.0013Thomas Heatherwick, opened 15 Mar 2019; cost estimated at up to $200M; 154 flights of stairs, 2,500 steps. Four people died by suicide there between Feb 2020 and Jul 2021; it closed, and reopened 28 Oct 2024 behind higher barriers. Developer Related Companies (Stephen Ross, host of a 2019 Trump fundraiser; Related invests in Equinox and SoulCycle). Hudson Yards: a press-estimated $25bn development on a railyard. The monument to going nowhere.
  • Vigeland Sculpture Park (Frognerparken), Oslo obelisk · 59.9271, 10.7013Gustav Vigeland: 212 bronze and granite sculptures. The Monolith: 14.12m granite column of 121 intertwined human figures - carved from single block over 14 years. Wheel of Life, Fountain of cosmic cycles. Entire human lifecycle depicted: birth, struggle, death, transcendence. The largest sculpture park by a single artist in the world. Vigeland's obsession: the human body as architecture of existence.
  • Walled Obelisk (Constantine's Obelisk), Istanbul Hippodrome obelisk · 41.0058, 28.9758The 32 m masonry 'Walled Obelisk', most likely built under Theodosius to mirror the Egyptian Obelisk of Theodosius at the other end of the Hippodrome spina, as Rome's Circus Maximus had two. In the 10th century Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus restored it and sheathed it in gilt bronze plates, later stripped. The masonry copy beside the Egyptian original.
  • Washington Monument, Washington D.C. obelisk · 1848-07-04 · 38.8895, -77.0353555 ft 5.125 in. Egyptian obelisk design - NPS: 'evoking timelessness of ancient civilizations'. Aluminum cap inscribed 'Laus Deo'. Masonic cornerstone July 4, 1848.
  • Wellington Testimonial (Wellington Monument), Phoenix Park, Dublin obelisk · 1817 · 53.3490, -6.3031At 62 m (203 ft), the granite obelisk to the Duke of Wellington, begun 1817 and completed only in 1861 due to funding shortfalls, is the tallest obelisk in Europe; its bronze relief plaques were cast from cannon captured at Waterloo. Source: Wikipedia, 'Wellington Monument, Dublin' / Buildings of Ireland.
  • Wilton Park (Wiston House) - Wiston, West Sussex governance · 1951 · 50.8998, -0.3590An executive agency of the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (formed 1946), based since 1951 at the 16th-century Wiston House, Wilton Park convenes over 70 strategic policy dialogues a year in the UK and overseas for officials and opinion-formers, in support of UK foreign policy.
  • Woody Island (Yongxing) - PLA Outpost, Paracel Islands military · 16.8340, 112.3430Woody Island (Yongxing), the largest of the disputed Paracels and seat of China's Sansha city, hosts an ~8,900-foot military-civil runway able to handle nuclear-capable H-6 bombers, plus reinforced hangars, radar sites and HQ-9 surface-to-air missile batteries, functioning as the administrative and military center of China's South China Sea presence. Source: CSIS (Gregory Poling); Newsweek; Radio Free Asia; CNBC.
  • World Economic Forum HQ - Cologny, Geneva governance · 1971 · 46.2247, 6.1922The WEF, founded by Klaus Schwab in 1971, runs from its lakeside headquarters at 91-93 Route de la Capite in Cologny, Geneva. It maintains a top 'Strategic Partner' tier of roughly 100 of the world's largest corporations that pay premium membership fees and shape its agenda. Source: World Economic Forum / Geneva Environment Network (genevaenvironmentnetwork.org).
  • Yokota Air Base, Tokyo, Japan military · 35.7485, 139.3487USFJ headquarters and Fifth Air Force. Located in western Tokyo - the capital of a sovereign nation hosts foreign military command. Yokota controls the airspace over greater Tokyo. Japanese commercial aircraft route around U.S. military airspace over their own capital.
  • Yulin Naval Base, Hainan, China military · 18.2200, 109.5500PLA Navy South Sea Fleet base at Sanya. Its eastern extension, Longpo (Yulin-East) on Yalong Bay, hosts the nuclear submarines (reported: Type 094 Jin-class SSBNs) and aircraft carriers.
  • Île Longue SSBN Base - Brest, France military · 1965 · 48.3043, -4.5081Selected by Charles de Gaulle in 1965 and operational since 1972, Île Longue in the Brest roadstead is the main base for France's Force Océanique Stratégique — its four Triomphant-class ballistic-missile submarines — and stores the warheads and missile fuel. Around 2,400 military and civilian personnel staff one of France's most sensitive sites. Source: GlobalSecurity.org, 'l'Ile Longue'; Naval Technology.

Section VIII - 17 locations

  • Alcor, Scottsdale, Arizona crypto-tech · 33.6174, -111.9109Alcor Life Extension Foundation. Finney's body cryopreserved at -196°C. Bitcoin's first transaction recipient is stored in a desert facility. Peter Thiel also reportedly signed up for cryopreservation.
  • Bitmain HQ, Beijing, China crypto-tech · 39.9581, 116.2924Beijing-based Bitmain has been the dominant maker of Bitcoin-mining ASICs, at its peak credited with a large majority of the market (share estimates vary) for mining rigs through its Antminer brand, and it operates Antpool, one of the largest mining pools. Its dominance means even 'Made in USA' Bitcoin largely runs on Chinese-designed hardware. Source: Bloomberg (2024); Wikipedia: Bitmain.
  • Bletchley Park, Milton Keynes, UK crypto-tech · 51.9981, -0.7411Bletchley Park was Britain's WWII codebreaking center, where Alan Turing and colleagues broke the German Enigma and Lorenz ciphers and built Colossus, the world's first programmable electronic digital computer. It is a foundational site of modern cryptography and computing, kept secret for decades after the war. Source: UK National Museum of Computing / Bletchley Park Trust.
  • Chainalysis HQ, New York crypto-tech · 40.7378, -73.9917Chainalysis is the leading blockchain-forensics firm, tracing crypto transactions for law enforcement and governments in over 70 countries; its clients include the FBI, DEA, IRS Criminal Investigation and the UK National Crime Agency, making it a central node in state surveillance of cryptocurrency flows. Source: Wikipedia: Chainalysis; Chainalysis Government Solutions.
  • Ekibastuz Bitcoin Mining Hub, Kazakhstan crypto-tech · 2021-05 · 51.7276, 75.3289After China banned crypto mining in May 2021, coal-rich Ekibastuz became a magnet for relocating miners, briefly helping push Kazakhstan to the world's second-largest Bitcoin hash rate; the local Enegix facility alone was built to power over 50,000 ASICs at 150 MW, roughly five times the town's own peak demand, straining the national grid. Source: MIT Technology Review (2023); Rest of World; Bitcoin Magazine.
  • El Zonte, El Salvador - Bitcoin Beach crypto-tech · 2019 · 13.4975, -89.3864Origin of El Salvador's Bitcoin adoption. Anonymous donor seeded BTC in fishing village (2019). President Bukele made BTC legal tender (2021). Chivo wallet - government-run Bitcoin wallet. Legal-tender status rescinded Feb 2025 under the IMF deal. Village experiment scaled to national policy, then rolled back.
  • FTX / Albany Resort, Nassau, Bahamas crypto-tech · 2022-11 · 25.0608, -77.3067FTX moved its headquarters to Nassau in 2021 and collapsed in November 2022 in one of history's largest financial frauds; founder Sam Bankman-Fried ran the empire from a roughly $40 million penthouse at the gated Albany resort and was later convicted on seven counts and sentenced to 25 years. FTX left an $8 billion customer shortfall. Source: Rolling Stone / Forbes / Time (2022); U.S. v. Bankman-Fried.
  • Genesis Block Café, Hong Kong crypto-tech · 2009-01-03 · 22.2816, 114.1545Named after Bitcoin's first block (Jan 3, 2009). Hong Kong: global crypto trading hub before 2023 regulatory shifts. Proximity to mainland China - where 65%+ of Bitcoin mining once concentrated before the ban.
  • Glen Park Branch Library, San Francisco (Silk Road Arrest) crypto-tech · 2013-10 · 37.7340, -122.4336In October 2013 the FBI arrested Ross Ulbricht, the 'Dread Pirate Roberts' behind the Bitcoin-powered darknet market Silk Road, at this branch library while he was logged into the site's admin panel. He was sentenced to life before receiving a full presidential pardon in January 2025. Source: KQED (2013 SF sting); NBC News; Glen Park Association.
  • Ledger HQ, Paris, France crypto-tech · 2020 · 48.8664, 2.3414Paris-based Ledger is the leading maker of hardware wallets for securing crypto private keys offline, having sold more than 7.5 million devices across 200 countries with over 20% of the world's crypto assets reportedly secured on its hardware. A 2020 data breach exposed customer emails, and for a subset names, postal addresses and phone numbers (Ledger). Source: Decrypt ('Ledger Unveils New Global Headquarters in Paris'); Ledger careers.
  • Mt. Gox Office, Cerulean Tower, Shibuya, Tokyo crypto-tech · 2014-02 · 35.6556, 139.7009The Shibuya-based Mt. Gox exchange handled over 70% of all global Bitcoin transactions before it collapsed in February 2014, having lost roughly 850,000 BTC (worth hundreds of millions then, tens of billions later) to theft and mismanagement. Protesters gathered outside its Tokyo office as it filed for bankruptcy. Source: Wikipedia: Mt. Gox; Japan Times (Mt. Gox coverage).
  • New Jersey Turnpike - Nash Crash Site crypto-tech · 2015-05-23 · 40.3032, -74.5169May 23, 2015: John Nash and wife Alicia killed in taxi crash returning from Norway (Abel Prize). Nash proposed 'Ideal Money' - a currency standard pegged to an industrial consumption price index; reading it as a description of Bitcoin is later commentary, not his claim. Both ejected - not wearing seatbelts.
  • Riot Platforms Rockdale Facility (Whinstone), Texas crypto-tech · 2021 · 30.6549, -97.0058Built on an abandoned aluminum smelter, Riot Platforms' Rockdale site is the largest single Bitcoin-mining facility by developed capacity in North America at about 700 MW, and Greenpeace calls it the most energy- and carbon-intensive Bitcoin mine in the US. Riot acquired builder Whinstone for $651 million in 2021. Source: Greenpeace USA; Global Energy Monitor (Whinstone Bitcoin mining facility).
  • Strategy (MicroStrategy) HQ, Tysons Corner, Virginia crypto-tech · 2025 · 38.9191, -77.2230Founded by Michael Saylor, the software firm rebranded from MicroStrategy to 'Strategy' in 2025 and is the world's largest corporate Bitcoin holder, having amassed roughly 597,000 BTC (worth over $70 billion in mid-2025) funded largely through equity and debt issuance. It pioneered the Bitcoin corporate-treasury model. Source: Virginia Business; Bitcoin Treasuries; Wikipedia: MicroStrategy.
  • Temple City, California - Hal Finney crypto-tech · 2009 · 34.1073, -118.0579Hal Finney lived here for about ten years, a few blocks from Dorian Satoshi Nakamoto (Forbes, 2014). Received first Bitcoin transaction from Satoshi (2009). Created first reusable proof-of-work system (RPOW). Finney died 28 Aug 2014 (ALS).
  • Volcano Bond Site, Conchagua, El Salvador crypto-tech · 13.2756, -87.8469Proposed 'Bitcoin City' at base of Conchagua volcano. Geothermal-powered Bitcoin mining. Proposed $1B 'Volcano Bond' (tokenized sovereign debt), postponed in March 2022. The volcano as power source for a digital currency city that hasn't been built.
  • Zug, Switzerland - Crypto Valley crypto-tech · 47.1660, 8.5155Self-proclaimed 'Crypto Valley.' Ethereum Foundation HQ. Bitcoin Suisse. Cardano Foundation. Polkadot. A low-tax Swiss canton. The offshore finance model applied to cryptocurrency - same geography, updated product.

Section IX - 154 locations

  • 816 Nuclear Military Plant, Chongqing, China underground · 1966 · 29.5569, 107.5072Underground plutonium-production complex near Fuling, Chongqing, begun 1966 (Third Front) by more than 60,000 PLA engineering soldiers; cancelled February 1984 when nearly complete and never operated. Declassified 2002; opened to tourists 2010.
  • ASML Headquarters - Veldhoven, Netherlands technology · 2019 · 51.4044, 5.4170ASML is the only firm on Earth able to build extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines — bus-sized systems priced around €150 million each — and holds effectively 100% of the EUV market; the Netherlands has barred EUV exports to China since 2019 under US pressure, making Veldhoven a linchpin of the global chip war. Source: Silicon Canals / Wikipedia (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASML).
  • Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station (US) military · -89.9830, 0.0000Geographic South Pole. NSF research station; IceCube Neutrino Observatory uses the 2-mile ice sheet to detect neutrinos. Supplied by New York Air National Guard LC-130 flights from McMurdo.
  • Antaviliai, Lithuania blacksite · 2018 · 54.7980, 25.4030Former riding school converted to CIA detention facility. Confirmed ECHR 2018. Another EU/NATO state hosting black sites.
  • Balaklava Submarine Base, Crimea underground · 44.4986, 33.5970Object 825 GTS: Soviet submarine base inside Tavros mountain with exits on both sides and a canal to the open sea; caisson gates could seal it; built to protect crews from nuclear fallout. Closed 1993; now a naval museum.
  • Beijing Underground City underground · 1969 · 39.9042, 116.4074Civil-defence tunnel network built 1969-79 on Mao's order during the Sino-Soviet border crisis, dug by more than 300,000 local citizens; the plan was to move half of Beijing's population underground.
  • Bunker-42 (Tagansky Protected Command Point), Moscow underground · 1950 · 55.7417, 37.6493A 7,000-square-metre command complex, 'Facility-02,' built from 1950 on Stalin's orders 65 metres beneath Moscow near Taganskaya metro, intended as a bomb-proof refuge and command post for Soviet strategic nuclear-armed bombers. Staff were reportedly bused in windowless vehicles and kept unaware of its location; it now operates as a Cold War museum. Source: Rusmania (rusmania.com); Wikipedia, 'Tagansky Protected Command Point'.
  • Burlington / Corsham, Wiltshire, UK underground · 51.4327, -2.1878Central Government War Headquarters: 35-acre complex ~120 ft underground in former Corsham stone quarries, for up to 4,000 officials. Decommissioned December 2004.
  • CFB North Bay - NORAD Underground, Ontario underground · 1959 · 46.3600, -79.4200Canadian NORAD Underground Complex, 60 storeys (~600 ft) underground. Built 1959-63; operations from 1 Oct 1963 until October 2006, when air-defence operations moved to a new surface building. Regional HQ moved to Winnipeg in 1997.
  • CFB Suffield / DRDC Suffield, Alberta military · 50.2700, -111.0000Largest army training area in Canada (~2,690 km²); home of the British Army Training Unit Suffield. Expropriated in 1941 for British chemical-warfare experiments. DRDC Suffield is Canada's lead laboratory for chemical and biological defence research.
  • CFS Debert Emergency Government HQ, Nova Scotia underground · 45.4369, -63.4565Regional Emergency Government Headquarters ('Diefenbunker') of CFS Debert, built in the 1960s; CFS Debert closed in the mid-1990s and was decommissioned in 1998. (HMCS Trinity, the naval ocean-surveillance unit, is at CFB Halifax.)
  • COFAS, Taverny, France underground · 49.0175, 2.2028Headquarters of the Strategic Air Forces Command (France's air-launched nuclear force) 1964-2007 and again since 2024, with a hardened command centre 70-80 m below ground in a former gypsum quarry.
  • Caltech - California Institute of Technology, Pasadena technology · 1946 · 34.1377, -118.1253Caltech manages JPL, a NASA FFRDC. Jack Parsons, a principal founder of JPL and Aerojet, led the Agape Lodge of Crowley's Thelema in Pasadena and performed the 'Babalon Working' with L. Ron Hubbard (1946); he died in a 1952 explosion ruled accidental. JPL later built the Ranger and Surveyor probes that scouted the Moon for Apollo.
  • Camp David, Maryland governance · 39.6484, -77.4650Presidential retreat on Catoctin Mountain. Raven Rock (Site R), the alternate military command center, lies about 6 miles away; an underground corridor between them is rumoured, not documented.
  • Camp Hero / Montauk AFS, Long Island military · 1942 · 41.0711, -71.8573Montauk Air Force Station (Camp Hero), 1942-1981. Joined SAGE in 1958; its AN/FPS-35 radar (126-ft reflector) became operational in 1960 and was abandoned in place when the station closed in January 1981. The 'Montauk Project' mind-control story is folklore with no documentary support.
  • Camp Lemonnier, Djibouti military · 11.5469, 43.1464U.S. base leased from Djibouti in 2002; supports CIA and DoD counter-terrorism and drone operations in Yemen and Somalia. Djibouti is listed among states reported to have assisted CIA rendition (attributed).
  • Carlsbad Caverns, New Mexico underground · 1978 · 32.1753, -104.4439119 known caves in a Permian reef (~265 million years). The Big Room - almost 4,000 ft long, 255 ft high - is the largest cave chamber in North America. Nearby Lechuguilla Cave is 1,588 ft deep, seventh-deepest in the U.S. Marked on a 1978 'Inner-Earth' map.
  • Cassidy International Airport, Kiritimati (Christmas Island) airport · 1957 · 1.9862, -157.3500Kiritimati (Christmas Island). British Operation Grapple (1957-58): nine tests at Malden Island and Kiritimati. U.S. Operation Dominic (1962): airdrop tests off Christmas Island. Servicemen and islanders exposed to radiation. Population 7,369 (2020); the whole island is a wildlife sanctuary.
  • Chaco Canyon, New Mexico underground · 36.0604, -107.9613UNESCO World Heritage. Ancestral Puebloan centre (c. 850-1250 CE): great houses with subterranean kivas, some aligned to solstices; prehistoric roads radiate to outlying sites. Labeled a 'suspected ancient tunnel site' on a Four Corners map.
  • Channel Tunnel (Chunnel), UK-France underground · 1994 · 51.0125, 1.486150.45 km, up to 75 m below the seabed; two rail tunnels and a service tunnel; the longest undersea section of any tunnel. Opened 1994.
  • Chelyabinsk-40 / Ozersk, Russia (Mayak) underground · 1957 · 55.7130, 60.7050Mayak plutonium complex. Kyshtym disaster (1957), the only INES Level 6 accident and third-worst after Chernobyl and Fukushima: 270,000+ people affected, 10,000-12,000 evacuated. Waste dumped in the Techa River and Lake Karachay, once lethal within an hour at its shore; the lake has since been infilled. Closed city.
  • Cheyenne Mountain, Colorado underground · 1966 · 38.7446, -104.8467NORAD/USNORTHCOM alternate command center under ~2,000 ft of granite; ~5.1 acres. Built 1961-66, operational 1966. 2015: $700M Raytheon contract to move communications systems into the EMP-hardened complex (Adm. Gortney).
  • China Jinping Underground Laboratory (CJPL), Sichuan underground · 2023-12 · 28.1532, 101.7114Now the world's deepest and largest underground laboratory, sited beside a hydropower traffic tunnel under 2,400 m of rock beneath Jinping Mountain; its CJPL-II expansion, operational December 2023, spans about 330,000 cubic metres and overtook Italy's Gran Sasso in both depth and volume. It houses the PandaX and CDEX dark-matter searches. Source: Scientific American; Wikipedia, 'China Jinping Underground Laboratory'.
  • China Lake NAWS, Ridgecrest, California military · 2019-07 · 35.6856, -117.69241.1 million acres - the U.S. Navy's largest single landholding (85% of its land for weapons R&D). Navy since 1943. The July 2019 Ridgecrest earthquakes (M6.4, M7.1) struck largely within the base; the M7.1 was California's strongest since 1999. Marked on 1978 and 1996 'underground base' maps.
  • Clear Space Force Station, Alaska military · 64.2950, -149.1950AN/FPS-132 UEWR missile warning radar. NORAD ballistic missile detection. Ground-based midcourse defense architecture. Northern early warning line.
  • Columbia University, New York, NY technology · 1942 · 40.8075, -73.9626Early Manhattan Project research at Columbia (Pupin Hall, 1939-42; later SAM Laboratories). New York State Psychiatric Institute, a Columbia affiliate: tennis player Harold Blauer died there in January 1953 after injections of a mescaline derivative in an Army Chemical Corps experiment. Zbigniew Brzezinski: Columbia professor, then Carter's National Security Advisor during the covert aid to the Afghan mujahideen.
  • Concordia Station, Antarctica (France/Italy) military · -75.1000, 123.3500Dome C, East Antarctic Plateau. ESA Mars conditions analog - testing Mars habitation protocols in Antarctica. The space agency rehearses planetary colonization at the bottom of this planet.
  • Coober Pedy, South Australia underground · 1915 · -29.0135, 134.7544Opal-mining town founded 1915. Many residents live in 'dugouts' below ground to escape the heat; underground churches, hotels and shops. Population 1,437 (2021). Marked on an underground-city map.
  • Củ Chi Tunnels, Vietnam underground · 11.1415, 106.4635Viet Cong tunnel network (~250 km) with hospitals, command posts and living quarters. U.S. and Australian 'tunnel rat' specialists fought inside; tunnels were attacked with gas, water, explosives and bombing.
  • DARPA Headquarters - Arlington, Virginia, USA technology · 1958-02-07 · 38.8787, -77.1086The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, created February 7, 1958 in response to Sputnik, funds the Pentagon's emerging-technology research (its ARPANET work seeded the internet). Its 13-story, 353,000 sq ft Ballston headquarters at 675 North Randolph Street meets DoD anti-terrorism standards with an 82-foot secured perimeter. Source: Wikipedia / CoStar (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DARPA).
  • DMZ Tunnels, Korean Peninsula underground · 1974 · 37.9164, 126.6986Four North Korean infiltration tunnels found since 15 Nov 1974. Third Tunnel: 1,635 m long, ~73 m deep; visitor information says it could move 30,000 men per hour. North Korea first denied it, then called it a coal mine; the rock is granite.
  • Denver International Airport (DIA) airport · 1994-03-19 · 39.8561, -104.6737Opened 28 Feb 1995, 16 months late, at a cost of $4.8B - nearly $2B over budget. 33,531 acres. Dedication capstone dated March 19, 1994 ('New World Airport Commission'). Blue Mustang ('Blucifer'), 32 ft, killed its sculptor Luis Jiménez when a section fell on him. Automated underground baggage system abandoned. Leo Tanguma murals.
  • Derinkuyu Underground City, Cappadocia, Turkey underground · 38.3736, 34.7344Excavated to ~85 m, with rolling stone doors; large enough for as many as 20,000 people with livestock and stores. Linked to Kaymakli by 8-9 km of tunnels. Carved from volcanic tuff; fully formed in the Byzantine era.
  • Detention Site Black, Bucharest, Romania blacksite · 2018 · 44.4268, 26.1025ECHR, Al Nashiri v. Romania (31 May 2018): Romania hosted a CIA secret prison, 'Detention Site Black', Sept 2003 - Nov 2005, and was complicit in the ill-treatment held there. The 2014 Senate report places Al Nashiri in Bucharest. Exact building not established here; Mihail Kogălniceanu airbase was a reported flight point, not the established detention site.
  • Diefenbunker, Ottawa, Canada underground · 1959 · 45.3510, -76.0457CFS Carp Emergency Government Headquarters, built 1959-61. Now Diefenbunker: Canada's Cold War Museum.
  • Diego Garcia, British Indian Ocean Territory military · 1968 · -7.3195, 72.4229UK territory leased to the U.S. The UK admitted (Feb 2008) that two U.S. rendition flights refuelled here in 2002; detention on the island is alleged, not established. Chagossians expelled 1968-1973 to make way for the base. 2025 treaty transfers sovereignty to Mauritius, base retained for 99 years.
  • Dugway Proving Ground, Utah military · 2011 · 40.1756, -112.9336Army chemical and biological test range since 1942, 801,505 acres. 1968 Dugway sheep incident. Project SHAD-era open-air tests in the 1960s. On 26 Jan 2011 the base locked down when a vial of VX was temporarily lost; it was recovered the next day.
  • Dulce, New Mexico - Archuleta Mesa underground · 36.9336, -106.9989Alleged underground base beneath Archuleta Mesa on the Jicarilla Apache Nation reservation - a claim with no documentary support at any tier. About 80 miles north of Los Alamos National Laboratory.
  • Dulles International Airport (IAD), Virginia airport · 38.9531, -77.4565About 17 miles (27 km) from CIA headquarters at Langley. Named for John Foster Dulles, Secretary of State and brother of CIA Director Allen Dulles (Iran 1953, Guatemala 1954 coups; plot against Lumumba in Congo). Rendition aircraft reported to have used Dulles (attributed).
  • Edinburgh Vaults, Scotland underground · 1788 · 55.9490, -3.1883South Bridge Vaults: about 120 rooms in the nineteen arches of South Bridge (completed 1788), used for taverns, workshops and lodgings for about 30 years, then abandoned. Nearby Mary King's Close, a 17th-century street, lies beneath the former Royal Exchange (City Chambers).
  • Eloy Alfaro Air Base (FOL Manta), Ecuador airport · 1999 · -0.9458, -80.6786From 1999 to 2009 the U.S. ran this coastal base as a Forward Operating Location, flying E-3 Sentry and P-3 Orion surveillance missions across a 6,400 km swath feeding intelligence to Joint Interagency Task Force South; Manta flights accounted for about 60% of eastern-Pacific drug interdictions before Ecuador declined to renew the lease. Source: GlobalSecurity.org, 'Eloy Alfaro Air Base / FOL Manta'; Air & Space Forces Magazine.
  • Esrange Space Center, Kiruna, Sweden satellite · 67.8933, 21.1042Rocket range and satellite ground station ~40 km east of Kiruna, above the Arctic Circle; owned and operated by SSC Space. Hosts ESA and commercial programmes.
  • Fort Greely, Alaska - Missile Defense military · 63.9950, -145.7370Ground-based Midcourse Defense (GMD) operational interceptors. Anti-ballistic missile shield's northern component. The missiles that defend against missiles, stationed in permafrost.
  • Gaza Tunnel Network, Rafah Crossing underground · 2023 · 31.2475, 34.2522Smuggling tunnels under the Egypt-Gaza border at Rafah, dug since the early 1980s, numbered about 1,200 before Egypt's military destroyed most of them in 2013-14. Hamas's combat tunnel network inside Gaza grew from that expertise; Israel's 2023-24 ground operation targeted it.
  • Georgetown University, Washington D.C. technology · 1950 · 38.9076, -77.0723Georgetown's Walsh School of Foreign Service: training ground for U.S. diplomats and national-security officials. Center for Security and Emerging Technology (2019): AI and security think tank funded by Open Philanthropy and others. Alumnus Bill Clinton (SFS '68).
  • Gotthard Base Tunnel, Switzerland underground · 2016 · 46.8300, 8.6500World's longest railway tunnel: 57.09 km, up to 2,300m below the Alps. Opened 2016, cost CHF 12.2B. Opening ceremony widely discussed for its theatrical production. Connects northern and southern Europe's rail logistics through the mountain the Swiss built their National Redoubt inside.
  • Gran Sasso National Laboratory (LNGS), Assergi underground · 1987 · 42.4211, 13.5162INFN laboratory beside the Gran Sasso highway tunnel under ~1,400 m of rock, operational since 1987; three main halls, 180,000 m³ in total. Dark-matter and neutrino experiments; endpoint of the 2011 CERN-OPERA neutrino-speed measurement. Long the world's largest underground lab, a title China's CJPL-II now claims.
  • Groom Lake / Area 51 Airstrip, Nevada airport · 1955 · 37.2350, -115.8111CIA/USAF classified flight test facility. U-2, A-12 (OXCART) and F-117 tested here. JANET flights carry workers from Las Vegas. CIA publicly acknowledged the base on 25 June 2013 through a FOIA release. On land the Western Shoshone hold was never ceded under the 1863 Treaty of Ruby Valley (their position).
  • HAARP, Gakona, Alaska military · 2015 · 62.3907, -145.1500High-frequency Active Auroral Research Program. 3.6 MW, 180 antenna array. Originally DARPA/Air Force/Navy. Transferred to University of Alaska Fairbanks (2015). Ionospheric heater: communications disruption, over-the-horizon radar, ELF submarine communication. Transfer to university changed FOIA jurisdiction, not capability.
  • Harvard Law School, Cambridge, MA governance · 1964 · 42.3770, -71.1167Dershowitz joined the Harvard Law faculty in 1964; full professor in 1967 at 28, then the youngest in the school's history; Felix Frankfurter Professor of Law from 1993; retired 2013.
  • Harvard University, Cambridge, MA technology · 1959 · 42.3770, -71.1167Henry Murray (OSS assessment veteran) ran stress experiments on undergraduates in 1959-62, recognised as purposefully abusive; Ted Kaczynski spent ~200 hours in the study (CIA funding alleged, not established). Timothy Leary and Richard Alpert's Harvard Psilocybin Project, 1960-62. Henry Kissinger: Harvard professor, then National Security Advisor and Secretary of State.
  • Hezbollah Tunnel Network, Southern Lebanon underground · 2018 · 33.0985, 35.2030Israel's Operation Northern Shield (Dec 2018 - Jan 2019) found and destroyed six Hezbollah cross-border attack tunnels from southern Lebanon.
  • Huawei Ox Horn Campus - Dongguan, China technology · 2019 · 22.8804, 113.8819Huawei's ~300-acre R&D campus on Songshan Lake, opened June 2018 at a cost of ~US$1.5 billion, is built as 12 villages replicating European cities (Paris, Verona, Freiburg) linked by an imported Swiss red train, and houses tens of thousands of researchers at a company central to US–China tech-sanctions disputes. Source: Wikipedia / Yahoo Finance (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huawei_Ox_Horn_Campus).
  • ITER Fusion Reactor - Saint-Paul-lès-Durance, France technology · 43.7071, 5.7776The 35-nation ITER tokamak at Cadarache aims to produce 500 MW of fusion power from 50 MW of heating (gain of 10). Initial budget close to €6 billion; construction and operation now projected at €18-22 billion, with outside estimates of $45-65 billion that ITER disputes.
  • JASON - IDA / MITRE, McLean, VA technology · 1960 · 38.9339, -77.1773JASON: independent scientific advisory group founded 1960, 30-60 members, mostly physicists, meeting in an annual summer study. Known work: the Vietnam-era McNamara Line, nuclear-weapons issues, early global-warming and acid-rain studies. Administered through the MITRE Corporation; DoD ended the contract in April 2019, then reinstated it.
  • JASON Summer Study - La Jolla, CA technology · 32.8328, -117.2713JASON holds an annual summer study, historically in La Jolla, where its members - academics holding clearances - review problems for DoD, DOE and other sponsors.
  • Jerusalem Underground Command, Israel underground · 31.7683, 35.2137Crisis command center beneath the Judaean Mountains. Israeli continuity-of-government facility.
  • Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center, Inner Mongolia, China satellite · 40.9650, 100.2838China's first launch centre (Dong Fang Hong I, 1970; Shenzhou 5, 2003), in the Gobi across Ejin Banner (Inner Mongolia) and Jinta (Gansu); all Chinese crewed launches have left from here. Operated by the PLA.
  • Johns Hopkins University / APL, Laurel, MD technology · 2006 · 39.1667, -76.8978Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (1942): university-affiliated DoD research centre, budget ~$2.09B, 8,800 staff. Missile defence, Aegis, space systems, cyber. APL developed the WWII variable-time proximity fuze. Separately, Johns Hopkins Medicine's psilocybin research under Roland Griffiths (2006-2023).
  • Johnston Atoll, Pacific - Chemical/Military military · 1958 · 16.7295, -169.5339Remote Pacific atoll ~1,330 km WSW of Honolulu. U.S. nuclear tests (1958, 1962); biological-weapons testing; storage and destruction of chemical weapons until 2000. Now a National Wildlife Refuge, with plutonium clean-up on record.
  • Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Alaska military · 61.2530, -149.8070NORAD Alaska Region. Pacific Air Forces (11th Air Force). U.S. Army Alaska. Primary Arctic airpower projection. Joint base combining Air Force and Army at Alaska's population center.
  • K-116, Zlíchov, Prague, Czech Republic underground · 50.0624, 14.4025Cold War-era underground command bunker beneath Zlíchov hill. Eastern Bloc continuity infrastructure.
  • Kapustin Yar, Astrakhan Oblast, Russia military · 1946 · 48.5700, 45.7550Soviet rocket test range established 13 May 1946 using technology and specialists taken from defeated Germany; early Soviet ballistic-missile launches. Russia's original missile range.
  • Kaymakli Underground City, Cappadocia, Turkey underground · 38.4575, 34.7525Eight levels (four open). Connected to Derinkuyu by 8-9 km of tunnels. Used by Byzantine Christians as a refuge from Arab raids (780-1180); abandoned after the 1923 population exchange. Nearly a hundred tunnels still serve the village above.
  • Kelvedon Hatch Secret Nuclear Bunker, Essex underground · 1992 · 51.6743, 0.2547A three-storey Cold War bunker sunk about 125 feet under an ordinary-looking Essex bungalow, walls of 10 feet of reinforced concrete inside a Faraday cage, designed as a Regional Government Headquarters for up to 600 personnel (potentially including the Prime Minister) to administer survivors after a nuclear strike. Decommissioned in 1992 and now a museum. Source: Wikipedia, 'Kelvedon Hatch Secret Nuclear Bunker'; Nuclear Essex (nuclearessex.com).
  • Khost-Gardez Pass (K-G Pass), Afghanistan underground · 2009-12 · 33.5000, 69.5000Mountain road between Khost and Gardez, contested in turn by Soviet, mujahideen, Taliban and U.S. forces. FOB Chapman (CIA) near Khost: suicide bombing on 30 Dec 2009 killed seven Americans, CIA officers and contractors.
  • Klara Bunker, Stockholm, Sweden underground · 59.3293, 18.0686Capacity 8,000-12,000 people. Sweden has 65,000+ fallout shelters for 10 million population.
  • Kola Superdeep Borehole, Russia underground · 1970 · 69.3965, 30.6100Deepest human-made hole: 12,262 m true vertical depth, reached 1989. Drilling from 1970; stopped 1992 at 180°C against ~100°C expected; closed 1995. Penetrated about a third of the Baltic Shield crust; microscopic plankton fossils found 6 km down.
  • Kosvinsky Kamen, Urals, Russia underground · 59.5170, 59.0500Command-post bunker under ~300 m of granite (Jane's, 1994). U.S. analysts believe it houses the command post of Perimeter ('Dead Hand'), a semi-automatic retaliation system; accounts differ on whether launch still needs human approval once activated.
  • Kourou, French Guiana - Guiana Space Centre satellite · 5.1690, -52.6903Guiana Space Centre at Kourou, Europe's spaceport since 1968: ~5°N, near the equator, which raises payload to geostationary orbit; open sea to the east. Ariane 6 launches since July 2024.
  • Krasnoyarsk-26 / Zheleznogorsk, Russia underground · 56.2500, 93.5333Mining and Chemical Combine: plutonium reactors built in caverns in a granite mountain (AD 1958, ADE-1 1961, ADE-2 1965; last shut 2010); now stores spent fuel. The closed city also hosts ISS Reshetnev, Russia's largest satellite maker.
  • Kwajalein Atoll / Reagan Test Site, Marshall Islands military · 1946 · 8.7200, 167.7300U.S. Army missile testing facility. Space Fence radar installation. 67 nuclear tests on Bikini and Enewetak atolls (1946-58) - Marshallese people permanently displaced. Compact of Free Association gives U.S. military access in exchange for aid. Nuclear testing victims still seeking compensation.
  • Lalibela Rock-Hewn Churches, Ethiopia underground · 12.0319, 39.0472Eleven monolithic churches cut down into the bedrock (12th-13th century), connected by passages; UNESCO World Heritage. Bete Giyorgis is cruciform, carved ~40 ft into a pit.
  • Lava Beds National Monument, California underground · 1872 · 41.7142, -121.5076Hundreds of lava-tube caves on the flank of Medicine Lake Volcano, ~40 miles NE of Mount Shasta. In the Modoc War (1872-73) Kintpuash (Captain Jack)'s band held the lava beds against the U.S. Army for months before defeat. Marked on a 1978 'Inner-Earth' map.
  • Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, Livermore, CA technology · 2022-12-05 · 37.6900, -121.7100Nuclear-weapons laboratory founded 2 Sept 1952 (Lawrence and Teller). Designed the W87 (Minuteman III) and later W80 variants. Its National Ignition Facility achieved fusion ignition on 5 Dec 2022: 3.15 MJ out from 2.05 MJ of laser energy. Run by UC until 2007, then by Lawrence Livermore National Security LLC.
  • Little Saint James Island, U.S. Virgin Islands enclave · 2023-05 · 18.3000, -64.825370-78 acres. A 2005 power and fibre-optic cable from St Thomas gave the island dedicated connections; a maintenance building has sally-port doors. Sold May 2023, with Great Saint James, to Stephen Deckoff's SD Investments for US$60 million; announced plan: a luxury resort.
  • Long Tieng (Lima Site 20A), Laos airport · 19.1078, 102.9235A CIA-run airbase and 'secret city' that was the unofficial headquarters of the Secret War in Laos; at its peak the single airstrip handled around 900 daily takeoffs and landings, making it one of the busiest airfields in the world, while the surrounding town of 40,000 never appeared on maps. Source: CNN Travel, 'Long Tieng, Laos: Once the most secret place on Earth'; Wikipedia / Long Tieng.
  • Los Alamos National Laboratory, NM technology · 1943 · 35.8800, -106.3060Manhattan Project laboratory (1943) under Oppenheimer; designed both Little Boy and Fat Man. The Trinity site is ~150 miles south. Still one of the two U.S. nuclear-weapons design laboratories. Los Alamos town: ~13,200 people (2020).
  • MIT - Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA technology · 1951 · 42.3601, -71.0942MIT Radiation Laboratory (WWII): radar. Lincoln Laboratory (1951): SAGE air defence, missile defence, space surveillance - DoD-funded. Instrumentation Lab (now Draper): Apollo, ICBM and Trident guidance. Epstein gave MIT 10 gifts totalling $850,000 (2002-2017); the nine after his 2008 conviction included $525,000 to the Media Lab (Goodwin Procter report, Jan 2020).
  • MITRE Corporation, Bedford, MA technology · 1958 · 42.4862, -71.2756Not-for-profit spun out of MIT Lincoln Laboratory in 1958 (SAGE engineers). Manages six federally funded R&D centres serving DoD, the FAA, the IRS and VA, DHS and others. Revenue $2.37B (2023). Administers the JASON advisory group.
  • Mammoth Cave, Kentucky underground · 1812 · 37.1862, -86.1004Longest known cave system in the world: more than 426 miles surveyed (2025). Several levels, underground rivers. Prehistoric Native mining; saltpeter mining for gunpowder in the War of 1812; tuberculosis hospital in the cave (1840s). Marked on a 1978 'Inner-Earth' map.
  • McMurdo Station, Antarctica (US) military · 1962 · -77.8460, 166.6680Ross Island. Largest community in Antarctica - ~1,000 in summer, up to 1,200. Run by the NSF's U.S. Antarctic Program with military logistics (Operation Deep Freeze); harbour and airfields. PM-3A nuclear reactor 1962-1972, removed after leaks. The Antarctic Treaty permits military personnel and equipment for scientific or peaceful purposes.
  • Mittelwerk / Mittelbau-Dora Underground V-2 Factory, Nordhausen underground · 1943 · 51.5345, 10.7507Underground factory in a former gypsum mine in the Kohnstein, built with slave labour from the Mittelbau-Dora camp to produce V-2 missiles and later V-1s. About 60,000 prisoners passed through the camp in 1943-45; around one in three (~20,000) died - more than the V-2 killed in its attacks.
  • Mont Verdun, near Lyon, France underground · 45.8735, 4.7780Air Base 942 Lyon-Mont Verdun: air defence and operations centre (CDAOA South sector, linked to NATO ACCS) with an underground alternate strategic command centre hardened against chemical and nuclear attack.
  • Moscow - Metro-2 / D-6 underground · 55.7558, 37.6173Officially unacknowledged deep metro, said to link the Kremlin, FSB headquarters, Vnukovo-2 government airport and an underground town at Ramenki. Russia has never confirmed it.
  • Moscow State University (MSU), Russia technology · 1953 · 55.7033, 37.5314Russia's flagship university; its main building (1953, 239 m spire) is the tallest of Stalin's 'Seven Sisters'.
  • Mount Pony Federal Reserve Bunker (Culpeper Switch), Virginia underground · 1969 · 38.4420, -77.9731A radiation-hardened 140,000-square-foot bunker excavated into Mount Pony in 1969 as the Federal Reserve's continuity-of-government center; it stored roughly USD 4 billion in shrink-wrapped currency to restart the economy after nuclear war and ran the 'Culpeper Switch' handling the Fed's national wire transfers from 1970-1988. Now the Library of Congress Packard Campus audio-visual archive. Source: Gizmodo/Paleofuture; FAS Nuclear Forces (nuke.fas.org); Wikipedia, 'National Audio-Visual Conservation Center'.
  • Mount Weather, Bluemont, Virginia underground · 39.0630, -77.8890Emergency Operations Center. FEMA High Point Special Facility. Classified continuity-of-government facility.
  • Mount Yamantau, Urals, Russia underground · 1997 · 54.2500, 58.1000Large excavation observed by U.S. satellite imagery into the late 1990s; purpose never disclosed. Russia (1996) declined to inform foreign media about 'facilities under construction'. A 1997 U.S. Congressional finding cited a 'deception and denial policy'. Closed town of Mezhgorye (formed 1995 from Beloretsk-15 and -16) serves the site.
  • Mt. Rainier, Washington underground · 1947 · 46.8523, -121.760314,411 ft, highest peak of the Cascades; summit steam caves. Kenneth Arnold's 1947 sighting near the mountain gave rise to the term 'flying saucers'. Paradise Ice Caves documented from 1908. Marked on a 1978 'Inner-Earth' map.
  • Mt. Shasta, Siskiyou County, California underground · 1978 · 41.4092, -122.194914,179 ft stratovolcano. Subject of a Lemuria legend that grew from an 1880s mention to a hidden-city story by 1925-31 (Cerve). Lava tubes on its flanks. Sacred to Native peoples. Marked as an 'entrance' on a 1978 'Inner-Earth' map (a private map, not a government one).
  • Mt. Taylor, New Mexico underground · 35.2733, -107.632311,301 ft; sacred to the Navajo (Tsoodził), Acoma, Laguna, Zuni and Hopi. The surrounding Grants belt was mined for uranium 1951-1989; Laguna Pueblo's Jackpile Mine (1953-1982) was then the world's largest open-pit uranium mine. Marked on a Four Corners map.
  • NSO Group Headquarters - Herzliya, Israel technology · 2010 · 32.1656, 34.8469The Israeli cyber-intelligence firm NSO Group, founded 2010, develops Pegasus — a zero-click smartphone spyware classified as a military export and licensed sale-by-sale by the Israeli government. Investigations documented its use against journalists, activists and Palestinian NGO staff, and the US blacklisted the company in 2021. Source: Wikipedia / Amnesty International / OCCRP Pegasus Project (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSO_Group).

  • Pinal Airpark (Marana), Arizona, USA airport · 32.5111, -111.3325During the Vietnam era, Marana was the headquarters of all CIA air operations and the main U.S. maintenance base for Intermountain Airlines, a CIA front supporting Air America; later acquired by Evergreen, it is today the world's largest commercial-aircraft storage and heavy-maintenance boneyard.   • Rideau Canal / Parliamentary Precinct Tunnels, Ottawa underground · 1826 · 45.4215, -75.6972Rideau Canal (UNESCO, 2007): built 1826-32 under Lt-Col John By as a military supply route avoiding the St Lawrence in case of U.S. invasion. 202 km. In winter part of it is a skating rink.

  • Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, India satellite · 13.7200, 80.2300India's primary spaceport, on a barrier island off the Bay of Bengal, from which ISRO launches its PSLV and GSLV/LVM3 rockets including the Chandrayaan and Mangalyaan interplanetary missions; the near-equatorial coastal site allows spent stages to drop safely over the sea. Every later capability in this section - the smart-city camera, the licence-plate reader, the biometric index - is the same operation performed faster and without the paper.
  • Integrated Joint Operations Platform (IJOP) - Xinjiang Public Security, Ürümqi surveillance · 2016 · 43.8244, 87.6139The IJOP is a predictive-policing system rolled out across Xinjiang after a 2016 directive, aggregating data from Wi-Fi sniffers, ID cards, cameras and checkpoints to flag Uyghurs for questioning and detention.   • Kodak Hawkeye Works, 1447 St Paul St, Rochester NY surveillance · 1995-02 · 43.1819, -77.6259Kodak's classified plant, and the reason Rochester belongs in this section. CORONA was operational 1960-72: over 100 spacecraft, more than 800,000 high-resolution images, declassified in February 1995. The returned negative was cut into manageable lengths, titled frame by frame, duplicated onto black-and-white print stock and boxed; a single mission's output shipped out of Rochester by the ton, including the special enlargements prepared to brief the president. THE END OF THE LINE: the NRO flew KH-11, the first American electro-optical satellite, in Dec 1976; the last KH-9 HEXAGON film-return vehicle was lost on launch in 1986.   • Laboratory for Laser Energetics (OMEGA), University of Rochester technology · 1970 · 43.1131, -77.6326Established 1970 and funded principally through the Department of Energy's National Nuclear Security Administration. TIER: the laboratory, the laser and the funding line are documented. ICF is dual-use by design - the same physics serves stewardship of the nuclear stockpile and civil fusion research - and this marker asserts nothing beyond that. The point for this map is structural: when Kodak's consumer half collapsed, the optics competence did not leave Rochester, it stayed in the defence-facing institutions.   • Musha Cay, Bahamas (David Copperfield) enclave · 2006 · 23.8930, -76.2610Privately owned island of about 700 acres in the Exuma Cays, 85 miles southeast of Nassau, owned by illusionist David Copperfield and let to one group of guests at a time.
  • Mustique, St. Vincent (The Mustique Company) enclave · 1960 · 12.8830, -61.1830About 1,400 acres. Colin Tennant developed it and gave Princess Margaret a 10-acre plot as a wedding present (1960) - a plot, never the island. In 1976 Tennant sold a 60% controlling interest in The Mustique Company to Venezuelan industrialists Hans Neumann and Alberto Vollmer. The island is owned by The Mustique Company, itself owned by the island's homeowners. No British royal has owned Mustique.
  • Nauru - Mining + Detention Island enclave · -0.5228, 166.93158.1 sq mi. Smallest republic. Phosphate mining stripped 80% of surface. Australia's offshore detention center - asylum seekers held on a stripped-mining island. Resource extraction and human containment share coordinates.
  • Necker Island, BVI (Richard Branson) enclave · 2017-02 · 18.5272, -64.358174 acres. Richard Branson saw it in 1978 and bought it about a year later from Lord Cobham for $180,000. Run as a Virgin Limited Edition resort. Barack and Michelle Obama visited as Branson's guests (Feb 2017). The Great House burned down after a lightning strike in Aug 2011; Hurricane Irma devastated the island in Sept 2017.
  • Niihau, Hawaii (Robinson Family) enclave · 1864 · 21.9000, -160.1700'The Forbidden Island.' 69.5 sq mi. Bought from King Kamehameha V in 1864 for $10,000 by Elizabeth Sinclair, whose descendants, the Robinsons, still own it. Population 84 (2020), Hawaiian-speaking. No paved roads, no running water, no power lines. Entry by invitation.
  • Norman's Cay, Exumas, Bahamas enclave · 1978 · 24.5950, -76.8200Carlos Lehder used the island as the Medellín Cartel's transshipment base for cocaine flown into the US, 1978 to about 1982, extending the airstrip to about 1,000 m and guarding it with armed men and dogs.
  • North Brother Island (Typhoid Mary Quarantine), New York enclave · 1938 · 40.8007, -73.8985This 20-acre East River island between the Bronx and Rikers held Riverside Hospital's quarantine station, where Mary Mallon ('Typhoid Mary') was confined against her will for roughly 26 years until her death in 1938. Abandoned since 1963, it is now a NYC Parks bird sanctuary closed to the public, with access only by permit and Parks escort. Source: All That's Interesting; Untapped New York.
  • North Sentinel Island, Andaman Sea enclave · 2018 · 11.5500, 92.2300Home of the Sentinelese, one of the last uncontacted peoples; their number is unknown (the 2001 census estimate was 39; other estimates run higher). India bars approach within five nautical miles. In 2018 American missionary John Allen Chau was killed after landing illegally. The modern world keeps trying.
  • Palmyra Atoll, Pacific (Nature Conservancy) enclave · 2000 · 5.8833, -162.0833The only incorporated US territory. Most of the land was bought in 2000 by The Nature Conservancy for US$30M from the Fullard-Leo family; now a wildlife refuge. Used in 1962 as an observation site for high-altitude nuclear tests over Johnston Atoll. Site of the 1974 Sea Wind case: the murder, and possible double murder, of a San Diego couple.
  • Peter Island, BVI (Van Andel family) enclave · 2024-12 · 18.3600, -64.58001,800 acres, the largest private island in the BVI. Owned by the Amway Corporation from 1978 until 2001, when full ownership passed to the Van Andel family, one of Amway's two founding families (the other is DeVos). Resort closed after Hurricane Irma (2017); reported reopened December 2024.
  • Pitcairn Island, South Pacific enclave · 1790 · -25.0660, -130.1005Settled in 1790 by Bounty mutineers and Tahitians; a UK overseas territory. Population about 35 (2023). In 2004 seven island men - a third of its male population - were tried on 55 charges of sexual offences against children and young adults; six were convicted. Six more men living abroad were tried in Auckland in 2005.
  • Poivre Atoll, Seychelles (IDC) enclave · -5.7500, 53.3100Amirantes atoll about 37 km south of d'Arros, managed by the state-owned Islands Development Company. Unpaved airstrip of about 1,100 m on Poivre Nord, served occasionally by IDC aircraft. Former coconut plantation. Coordinates approximate (atoll centroid).
  • Poveglia, Venice, Italy enclave · 1793 · 45.3830, 12.3330Quarantine station for incoming ships and cargo from the late 18th century; from 1922 a long-term care facility, described as a psychiatric hospital, closed 1968, then state property. In 2025 the northern part was granted to the association Poveglia per tutti for a public park.
  • Robben Island, South Africa (Mandela) enclave · 1964 · -33.8060, 18.3660Mandela imprisoned 18 years (1964-1982). Island-as-control pattern: powerful retreat to islands, inconvenient are confined on them. Same geography, inverse purpose.
  • Runit Dome, Enewetak Atoll, Marshall Islands enclave · 1980 · 11.5450, 162.3530Concrete cap built by the US in 1977-80 over a nuclear blast crater on Runit Island, entombing about 100,000 cubic yards of radioactive soil and debris from Enewetak tests. A 2013 DOE report found minor cracking, and that the soil around the dome is more contaminated than its contents; the concern is tidal groundwater moving beneath its unlined base. Marshallese officials and the UN have warned of leakage.
  • Rémire (Eagle) Island, Seychelles (IDC) enclave · -5.1167, 53.3117Amirantes island about 33 km north of d'Arros. Paved airstrip of about 460 m (ICAO FSSR), the shortest in the group. Reserved as a presidential retreat until 2010; since then run by the state-owned IDC, which opened a small guest house in 2012.
  • Skorpios, Greece (Onassis → Rybolovleva lease) enclave · 1963 · 38.6920, 20.7430About 206 acres (83.2 ha). Bought in 1963 by Aristotle Onassis, who married Jacqueline Kennedy here on 20 October 1968. In April 2013 Ekaterina Rybolovleva, daughter of Russian potash billionaire Dmitry Rybolovlev, bought companies from Athina Onassis's trust for $153 million, including a long-term lease of the island. Shipping dynasty to Russian potash fortune.
  • Snake Island (Zmiinyi), Ukraine enclave · 2022-02-24 · 45.2557, 30.2040'Russian warship, go f**k yourself.' Feb 24, 2022 - Ukrainian border guards defied Russian Navy cruiser Moskva. The cruiser later sank. Strategic Black Sea island fought over since antiquity.
  • Tagomago Private Island, Ibiza, Spain enclave · 2000 · 39.0333, 1.6500Tagomago is a roughly 600,000-square-metre privately owned islet about 900 m off Ibiza's east coast, marketed as one of the Mediterranean's most exclusive private-island rentals with a single luxury villa and a staff of around twelve reserved for one group at a time. It lies within the EU Natura 2000 protected network yet is held as a fully private retreat. Source: Rental Escapes; Tripadvisor (Tagomago Private Island Retreat).
  • Tetiaroa, French Polynesia (Brando) enclave · 1967 · -17.0200, -149.570012 motu, about 585 ha (1,450 acres) of land. The Tahitian royal family sold the atoll to dentist Johnston Walter Williams in 1904; Marlon Brando bought the motu from a Williams descendant in the late 1960s. Now The Brando resort, on islets held under a 99-year lease signed by Brando.
  • The Cloister, Sea Island, Georgia (2004 G8 Summit) enclave · 2004 · 31.1807, -81.3506The private barrier-island resort hosted the 30th G8 Summit on June 8-10, 2004, gathering leaders of the U.S., UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Canada and Russia at The Cloister; the G8 boardroom is still shown on resort tours. Sea Island is a gated enclave of estates that has drawn dignitaries since a 1928 visit by President Calvin Coolidge. Source: New Georgia Encyclopedia; George W. Bush White House Archives (g8/2004).
  • The World Islands, Dubai enclave · 25.2200, 55.1700About 300 artificial islands off Dubai shaped as a world map, built by Nakheel from 2003; work halted in the 2008 financial crisis and most islands remain undeveloped. The islands are sold as private real estate but remain UAE territory.
  • Île Sainte-Marguerite, France (Man in the Iron Mask) enclave · 1687 · 43.5170, 7.0470Fort Royal prison - Man in the Iron Mask held here 1687-1698. Historical precedent: islands as both sanctuary and prison. Same geography protects the powerful and imprisons the inconvenient.
  • Île d'Arros & St Joseph Atoll, Seychelles (Save Our Seas Foundation) enclave · 2012-08 · -5.4158, 53.3017Private island since 1975 (Prince Shahram Pahlavi Nia of Iran); bought by L'Oréal heiress Liliane Bettencourt in 1998 for US$18M; sold in Aug 2012 with St Joseph Atoll for US$60M, to be managed by the Save Our Seas Foundation; nature reserve since 2014. SOSF was founded in Geneva in 2003 by Saudi businessman Abdulmohsen Abdulmalik Al-Sheikh - Al ash-Sheikh, the clerical family, not Al Saud. 1.71 km2 with an unpaved airstrip; St Joseph lies 2.3 km east across a 1 km channel and has no strip.

Section XIII - 102 locations

  • 2001: A Space Odyssey - MGM-British Studios, Borehamwood technology · 1968 · 51.6608, -0.2592Stanley Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey (1968) was among the last films shot at MGM-British Studios. Its black monolith (1:4:9 proportions in Clarke's novel) appears at each evolutionary leap. Kubrick died of a heart attack in March 1999, six days after screening his final cut of Eyes Wide Shut.
  • Acropolis Museum, Athens museum · 2009 · 37.9685, 23.7284Built 2009, €130M. Entire floor designed with empty spaces — reserved for the Parthenon Marbles currently in the British Museum. Lord Elgin removed them 1801-1812 from the Parthenon under an Ottoman permit of questionable validity. Greece has demanded return since independence (1832). The museum that was architecturally designed around its own absence — the building is a repatriation argument.
  • Art Institute of Chicago museum · 1879 · 41.8796, -87.6237Founded 1879. One of the largest Impressionist collections outside Paris; Seurat's Sunday Afternoon, Wood's American Gothic. Board historically drawn from Chicago's industrial fortunes (Armour meat-packing, railroads, real estate), the same circle behind the 1893 World's Fair that also founded the nearby Field Museum.
  • Aswan Unfinished Obelisk, Egypt obelisk · 24.0772, 32.8942Would have been the largest obelisk ever: ~42 m and nearly 1,090 tonnes. Abandoned when cracks appeared during quarrying (15th century BC). Still lies in the quarry, carved directly from bedrock - the failure that explained the method.
  • Athens Olympic Complex - 2004 Summer Olympics financial · 2004 · 38.0362, 23.7874Cost the Greek state ~EUR 9bn. Most venues later abandoned (Hellinikon rusting). Popular accounts blame the Games for the 2010-18 debt crisis, but there is little evidence for a significant contribution - the debt (later ~180% of GDP) and Troika austerity had wider causes.
  • Baalbek, Lebanon archaeological · 34.0047, 36.2110Trilithon: three limestone blocks of ~800 t each, each over 19 m long, set in the Temple of Jupiter podium. In the nearby quarry lie the Stone of the Pregnant Woman (~1,000 t) and still larger unused blocks (~1,200 t and a block found in 2014). How Roman builders moved them is studied, not unexplained.
  • Bardo National Museum, Tunis museum · 2015-03-18 · 36.8094, 10.1342On March 18, 2015, gunmen attacked Tunisia's national museum - home to one of the world's great Roman mosaic collections - killing about 22 people, mostly foreign tourists. ISIS claimed it; Tunisian authorities attributed it to the al-Qaeda-linked Uqba ibn Nafi Brigade. It devastated the tourism sector.
  • Beijing National Stadium (Bird's Nest) - 2008 Summer Olympics surveillance · 2008 · 39.9929, 116.3966US$428M stadium. Mass displacement of hutong neighbourhoods; internet controls tightened; Tibet protests crushed in March 2008. Ai Weiwei, the stadium's artistic consultant, later distanced himself from it as part of a 'pretend smile'. The surveillance state dressed up as a sporting event.
  • Berlin Olympic Stadium - 1936 Summer Olympics governance · 1936 · 52.5147, 13.2395Nazi propaganda showcase. Jesse Owens won four gold medals; the story that Hitler refused his hand is a myth - Hitler had stopped publicly congratulating any winners, and Owens said 'Hitler didn't snub me - it was our president who snubbed me.' Leni Riefenstahl's Olympia pioneered sports-film technique. The Olympics as legitimisation of a fascist state. Stadium still in use.
  • Black Wall Street - Greenwood District, Tulsa OK conflict · 1921-05-31 · 36.1570, -95.9903Greenwood District, Tulsa - 'Black Wall Street', one of the wealthiest Black communities in the US. On 31 May-1 June 1921 white mobs, many deputised by city officials, burned more than 35 square blocks. Eyewitnesses describe private aircraft firing on and firebombing the district (attributed). Deaths: official count 36, estimates up to ~300; about 10,000 left homeless; property losses of ~$2.25M (1921). The National Guard interned up to 6,000 Black residents. A grand jury indicted more than 85 people but no one was convicted for the killings or destruction. The survivors' lawsuit was dismissed in 2024; in 2025 the city announced a $105M private trust for descendants.
  • Bouvet Island, South Atlantic military · 1979-09-22 · -54.4333, 3.4000Norwegian dependency, described as the world's most remote island - ~1,700 km from Queen Maud Land, Antarctica. On 22 Sept 1979 a US Vela satellite registered a double flash over the sea between Bouvet and the Prince Edward Islands (the Vela incident); it has been read as an Israeli-South African nuclear test, a meteoroid or an instrument glitch - contested, never confirmed.
  • British Museum, London museum · 1897 · 51.5194, -0.1270About 8 million objects. Holds the Parthenon (Elgin) Marbles, the Rosetta Stone and Benin Bronzes taken in the 1897 British punitive expedition; Greece and Nigeria have long sought return. The museum as colonial warehouse (the site's characterisation).
  • Caral-Supe, Barranca Province, Peru archaeological · 2009 · -10.8901, -77.5011Built around 2600 BC and home to over 3,000 people, Caral is the oldest known urban center in the Americas - roughly contemporary with the Egyptian pyramids - with six stepped platform mounds and sunken circular plazas of the Norte Chico civilization; UNESCO listed it in 2009. Source: Wikipedia, 'Caral' / Popular Archaeology.
  • Christie's, King Street, London - Major Auction House financial · 1766 · 51.5085, -0.1370Founded 1766. Owned by François Pinault through Groupe Artémis since 1998. Sold Leonardo's 'Salvator Mundi' for $450.3M (2017) to Prince Badr bin Abdullah, reported to be bidding for Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (attributed). High-end art moves through auctions, private sales and freeport storage with limited public visibility of owners.
  • Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, Bentonville, AR museum · 36.3824, -94.2028Alice Walton - Walmart heir (net worth ~$134bn, 2026). The Walton Family Foundation endowed Crystal Bridges with ~$800M for construction, acquisitions and operations, in Walmart's home town. Collection includes Durand, Rockwell, Warhol, Rothko. Walmart is the largest private US employer; studies have counted many of its workers on public assistance (attributed). Retail fortune converted into a tax-advantaged philanthropic institution.
  • Deutsches Museum, Munich museum · 48.1299, 11.5833World's largest museum of science and technology. 28,000+ objects. V-2 rocket on display — the weapon built by slave labor at Mittelbau-Dora (20,000 deaths). Werner von Braun artifacts. Enigma machines. The museum that displays the technology without the slaves who built it. Science and technology museums worldwide follow this template: celebrate the invention, omit the human cost.
  • El Obelisco, Avenida 9 de Julio, Buenos Aires obelisk · 1936-05-23 · -34.6037, -58.381671.5 m concrete obelisk built in 1936 for the 400th anniversary of the city's first founding, at the junction of Corrientes and the 9 de Julio, often called the widest avenue in the world. It stood through the 1976-83 junta, whose disappeared are estimated by human-rights groups at 30,000 (contested), and through repeated economic collapses.
  • Ellora Caves, Maharashtra, India archaeological · 20.0258, 75.178034 caves cut into basalt (AD 600-1000) - Hindu, Buddhist and Jain temples side by side. The Kailasa temple (Cave 16) was excavated vertically from the top of the rock downward; an estimated ~200,000 tonnes of rock were removed (estimate).
