DIA's own status brief records: performance 'has been excellent and they are in full compliance'; 12 project management plans and 26 detailed research reports delivered by 30 June 2009 - 'twice minimum requirement'; '$12 million for the continuation of this contract by DIA/DI has been submitted in the FY10 defense budget'; the contracting officer extended the contract to 30 September at no additional cost, and BAASS indicated willingness to operate 'at risk' in option year 1 until FY10 funds arrived. Deliverable titles include Warp Drives, Wormholes in Space Time, Antigravity Studies, Metamaterials and Invisibility, Brain-Machine Interfaces, and Field Effects on Biological Tissues; one author organisation survives redaction as Sandia. Redactions are marked (b)(3):10 USC 424, the statute shielding DIA organisational detail. TIER: the contract, the money and the report titles are documented in DIA's own release; the existence of recovered craft is NOT documented by any of it. Source: DIA FOIA reading room, AAWSAP/AATIP collection, Aerospace_Contract_Status_Bigelow_Aerospace_Advanced_Space_Studies.pdf.
  • C-130 60528 shootdown site, Sasnashen, Soviet Armenia military · 1958-09-02 · 40.3570, 43.99212 September 1958. FOIA-SOURCED (NSA reading room, read 18 Aug 2026). Soviet MiG-17 pilots shot down a US Air Force reconnaissance-configured C-130 over Soviet Armenia; all 17 crew were lost. NSA released roughly 13 documents in July 2021 - incident reports, Russian-language intercept transcripts with translations of the fighter pilots' own radio traffic during the engagement, audio files, crew and casualty records, and a survey of reconnaissance incidents 1949-1960. The intercepted cockpit traffic is the reason this case is unusual: the shootdown is documented from inside the attacking formation's own communications. Source: NSA Historical Releases - C130 Shootdown collection.
  • Chelmsford Private Hospital, Sydney, Australia blacksite · 1963 · -33.7380, 151.0710Chelmsford Private Hospital, Pennant Hills, Sydney. Harry Bailey's deep sleep therapy (1963-1979): patients kept unconscious for days or weeks with barbiturates, often with ECT. Between 24 and 26 patients died at the hospital; the treatment has been linked to 85 deaths including 19 suicides. Bailey had observed Ewen Cameron's and William Sargant's methods on a WHO fellowship. He died by suicide in 1985 while facing committal proceedings; the Chelmsford Royal Commission followed. Source: Wikipedia, Harry Bailey; Deep sleep therapy.
  • Colonia Dignidad, Chile blacksite · 1961 · -36.3869, -71.5881German enclave in Chile (founded 1961) run by Paul Schafer, a former Wehrmacht medic. It served as a DINA detention and torture site under Pinochet, a site of systematic child sexual abuse, an arms cache, and reportedly a laboratory for Project Andrea sarin. Schafer fled child-abuse charges in 1996, was arrested in Argentina in 2005 and died in a Chilean prison in 2010. Source: Wikipedia, Colonia Dignidad.
  • Defense Intelligence Agency HQ, Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling, DC military · 2009 · 38.8427, -77.0159FOIA-SOURCED (DIA reading room, read 18 Aug 2026). DIA headquarters, and the agency whose electronic reading room holds the AAWSAP/AATIP collection: 53 released items covering the Bigelow contract chain and 37 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents on subjects from inertial electrostatic confinement fusion to traversable wormholes. The collection also holds the paper trail of Senator Harry Reid's interest - memos on his visit to DIA, and his letter to the Deputy Secretary of Defense seeking Special Access Program status for the effort, which was reviewed and, per the same file series, not granted in the form requested. Other DIA reading-room collections indexed the same day: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena, POWs/MIA/Detainees, Weapons Development and Proliferation, China Mission Group, and annual FOIA request logs 2001-2023. Source: DIA FOIA Electronic Reading Room.
  • ESMA (Navy Mechanics School) - Argentine Dirty War, Buenos Aires blacksite · 1976 · -34.5431, -58.4627ESMA (Navy Mechanics School), Buenos Aires - the main clandestine detention and torture centre of Argentina's 1976-1983 dictatorship; an estimated 5,000 prisoners passed through, most disappeared, many killed in 'death flights' over the Rio de la Plata and Atlantic. Now the ESMA Museum and Site of Memory. CONADEP's 'Nunca Mas' (1984) documented 8,961 disappearances; human-rights organisations estimate 30,000.
  • Evin Prison, Tehran, Iran blacksite · 35.7961, 51.3841Iran's most notorious prison, at the foot of the Alborz Mountains in northwestern Tehran, holding activists, journalists and dual nationals; its Ward 209 is controlled directly by the Ministry of Intelligence and documented by Human Rights Watch for prolonged solitary confinement and 'white torture.' Source: Human Rights Watch, 'Like the Dead in Their Coffins' (2004); Wikipedia / Evin Prison.
  • Gulf of Tonkin, Vietnam - DESOTO patrol area military · 1964-08-04 · 20.5000, 107.50002-4 Aug 1964. FOIA-SOURCED UPGRADE (read directly from NSA's reading room, 18 Aug 2026). NSA released its Tonkin holdings in two tranches - 30 Nov 2005 and 30 May 2006 - and states on the release page that it was 'not NSA's intention to prove or disprove any one set of conclusions,' only to publish the material. The substantive finding is NSA historian Robert J. Hanyok's Cryptologic Quarterly study 'Skunks, Bogies, Silent Hounds, and the Flying Fish: The Gulf of Tonkin Mystery, 2-4 August 1964' (classified 2001, declassified Nov 2005): the 2 Aug attack happened; the 4 Aug attack did not; and the SIGINT product that appeared to confirm it was built from 4 Aug intercepts about recovery of the P-4s damaged on 2 Aug - re-dated, re-translated and selectively excerpted. PRECISION: that is Hanyok's conclusion, not an institutional NSA finding, and he describes a mix of analytic error and deliberate misrepresentation rather than a single fabrication order. Collection also holds CAPT J.J. Herrick, Col Ralph Steakley (DESOTO) and Lt Col Delmar C. Lang reports. Sources: nsa.gov Gulf of Tonkin release; rel1_skunks_bogies.pdf.
  • Hanslope Park - Migrated Archives / Operation Legacy, UK blacksite · 2011 · 52.0847, -0.8301FCDO site (also home to HM Government Communications Centre) where the 'migrated archives' were held: about 20,000 files from 41 former colonies, removed at independence. The FCO admitted holding them only in 2011, during the Mau Mau veterans' case (Mutua and others v FCO); they were moved to The National Archives (FCO 141). Operation Legacy was the Colonial Office programme to destroy or remove files that could embarrass Britain. Hanslope also held about 1.2 million other unreleased FCO records. Source: Wikipedia, Migrated Archives; Hanslope Park; Operation Legacy.
  • Holmesburg Prison, Philadelphia, USA blacksite · 1951 · 40.0371, -75.0188Between 1951 and 1974 University of Pennsylvania dermatologist Albert Kligman ran non-therapeutic experiments on inmates, most of them Black, exposing them to viruses, skin-blistering chemicals, radioactive isotopes, psychoactive drugs and dioxin, with sponsors including Dow Chemical and the US Army. Philadelphia formally apologised in 2022. Source: Wikipedia, Holmesburg Prison; Philadelphia Inquirer (Oct. 6, 2022).
  • In Ekker Nuclear Test Site, Algeria (French underground tests) military · 1962-05-01 · 24.0500, 5.050013 underground French nuclear tests (1961-1966). 'Béryl' test (May 1, 1962) - containment failure caused radioactive cloud to irradiate soldiers and officials including ministers. Footage suppressed for decades. French military personnel ordered to walk through contaminated zone. Algerian independence (1962) did not stop French testing - they continued for 4 more years under treaty provision. The colony that gained independence but not sovereignty over its own soil.
  • Kaechon Internment Camp (Camp 14), North Korea blacksite · 39.5711, 126.0556A roughly 155-square-kilometre 'total control zone' political prison on the north bank of the Taedong River, near Kaechon, South Pyongan, holding an estimated 15,000 prisoners for life; a UN Commission of Inquiry found extermination, enslavement and torture in North Korea's political prison camps. Tracked via satellite imagery by HRNK. Source: HRNK, 'North Korea Imagery Analysis of Camp 14'; Wikipedia, Kaechon internment camp.
  • Kamloops Indian Residential School, British Columbia blacksite · 2021-05 · 50.6797, -120.2950Kamloops Indian Residential School (opened 1890). In May 2021 the Tk'emlups te Secwepemc announced ground-penetrating radar results indicating about 200-215 probable unmarked burials in the orchard; the surveyor said only excavation could confirm human remains, and none has been reported. The NCTR documents 51 student deaths at the school. The residential school system (to 1996) took 150,000+ Indigenous children; the TRC (2015) found at least 4,100 died. Other 2021 GPR findings include Marieval (Cowessess First Nation, 751 graves). Source: Wikipedia, Kamloops Indian Residential School.
  • Katyn Forest, Russia (site of NKVD massacre) conflict · 1940-05 · 54.7723, 31.7858The NKVD executed about 22,000 Polish officers, police and intelligentsia (21,857 per Soviet documents) in April-May 1940. Germany announced the graves in 1943; the USSR blamed the Nazis and tried to charge Katyn at Nuremberg, where the case failed. The USSR acknowledged NKVD guilt only in 1990. Russia's own investigation was closed in 2004 with most of its 183 volumes classified; 137 were handed to Poland in 2010. Source: Wikipedia, Katyn massacre.
  • Maralinga Nuclear Test Site, South Australia military · 1956-09-27 · -30.1594, 131.6136British nuclear tests on Maralinga Tjarutja (Pitjantjatjara) land: Operation Buffalo from 27 September 1956 and further major and minor trials to 1963. Aboriginal people were not adequately protected; the 'black mist' accounts come from the earlier Emu Field tests (1953). The McClelland Royal Commission (1984-85) found significant residual contamination, including plutonium; contaminated soil and debris were buried in trenches. Source: Wikipedia, Maralinga.
  • Mururoa Atoll - French Nuclear Testing, French Polynesia military · 1966 · -21.8301, -138.9108France conducted 193 nuclear tests in French Polynesia (1966-1996) at Moruroa and Fangataufa - atmospheric until 1974, then underground; Moruroa alone accounts for 175-181. Soldiers, workers and Polynesian civilians were exposed; the state long denied health effects. The Morin law (2010) created a compensation scheme; INSERM published a collective expert report on health consequences in February 2021. The veterans' association Moruroa e Tatou documented contamination. Source: Wikipedia, Moruroa.
  • New York State Psychiatric Institute, Manhattan blacksite · 1953-01-08 · 40.8405, -73.9420New York State Psychiatric Institute (Columbia University affiliate). Tennis professional Harold Blauer, admitted for depression in late 1952, died on 8 January 1953 after injections of a mescaline derivative (EA-1298, MDA) in an Army Chemical Corps-contracted experiment run by Paul Hoch and James Cattell. His family learned the truth only in 1975. Source: Wikipedia, Harold Blauer; MKUltra.
  • Oak Ridge - Penetanguishene Mental Health Centre, Ontario blacksite · 1960 · 44.8008, -79.9294Maximum security psychiatric facility. Dr. Elliott Barker's 'total encounter capsule' program (1960s-1970s): patients locked naked in a room together for weeks under LSD, forced to undergo 'psychic driving' (borrowed from Cameron at Allan Memorial). Defense Research Board funded. Barker believed he could 'cure' psychopathy through forced intimacy under hallucinogens. The experiment that used one MKUltra technique to treat the damage caused by another.
  • Pavlov Institute of Physiology, St. Petersburg, Russia blacksite · 59.9718, 30.3218Pavlov Institute of Physiology (Russian Academy of Sciences), St Petersburg - named for Ivan Pavlov, whose work on conditioned reflexes became foundational to behavioural science. Soviet punitive psychiatry is a separate history (see Serbsky Center).
  • Pentagon, Washington D.C. military · 1962-03-13 · 38.8711, -77.0562Operation Northwoods: on 13 March 1962 the Joint Chiefs of Staff submitted to Defense Secretary McNamara proposals for false-flag acts - including staged attacks at Guantanamo, sinking refugee boats and terrorism in US cities - to justify an invasion of Cuba. The proposals were rejected by President Kennedy.
  • Porton Down - MoD Chemical/Biological Testing, Wiltshire, UK blacksite · 1953-05-06 · 51.1311, -1.7100UK Ministry of Defence chemical and biological research site. Up to 20,000 servicemen took part in trials (1949-1989; Operation Antler examined 1939-1989), many without proper informed consent, including nerve agents and, in MI6 tests, LSD. Leading Aircraftman Ronald Maddison died after sarin exposure on 6 May 1953; a 2004 inquest found unlawful killing. In 2008 the MoD paid 360 veterans 3 million pounds without admitting liability. Source: Wikipedia, Porton Down; Ronald Maddison.
  • Reggane - French Nuclear Tests in Algeria (Sahara) military · 1960-02-13 · 26.3117, -0.0572First French nuclear test 'Gerboise Bleue' (February 13, 1960) - 4x Hiroshima yield. 17 tests in the Algerian Sahara (1960-66) including 4 atmospheric. Local populations (including French soldiers) exposed without warning. Saharan communities still report elevated cancer rates. Files partially declassified 2013 - 53 years after first detonation. France conducted nuclear tests in its colony, then left.
  • Roodeplaat Research Laboratories - Project Coast, Pretoria, South Africa blacksite · 1983 · -25.5906, 28.3500Apartheid-era chemical and biological weapons programme (formed 1983 after a 1981 order) led by Wouter Basson, run through front companies including Roodeplaat Research Laboratories. It produced poisons and covert delivery devices; TRC testimony described research into anti-fertility agents aimed at the Black population and attempts to contaminate water with cholera. Much material was destroyed in the early 1990s. Basson was acquitted in 2002. Pin approximate. Source: Wikipedia, Project Coast.
  • Saydnaya Military Prison, Syria blacksite · 2011-09 · 33.6650, 36.3286Saydnaya military prison, about 30 km north of Damascus, where Amnesty International estimated 5,000-13,000 detainees were extrajudicially hanged between September 2011 and December 2015, calling it a 'human slaughterhouse'; groups of up to 50 at a time were taken from their cells for hanging. Opened by opposition forces on 8 December 2024. Source: Amnesty International (2017), via Wikipedia, Saydnaya Prison.
  • Serbsky State Scientific Center, Moscow, Russia blacksite · 1960 · 55.7256, 37.5997Serbsky Center, Moscow - the Soviet Union's central forensic psychiatry institute and a centre of punitive psychiatry. Dissidents were diagnosed with 'sluggish schizophrenia', a diagnosis used almost only in Soviet psychiatry. Gen. Pyotr Grigorenko was declared insane there because he 'was unshakably convinced of the rightness of his actions'. The number of political detainees committed is uncertain. Source: Wikipedia, Serbsky Center; Sluggish schizophrenia.
  • Spring Grove State Hospital, Catonsville, MD blacksite · 1963 · 39.2724, -76.7358Spring Grove Hospital Center, Catonsville, Maryland - founded 1797, the second-oldest continuously operating psychiatric hospital in the US. From 1963 to 1976 researchers including Stanislav Grof and Walter Pahnke gave LSD and other psychedelics to patients, including terminally ill cancer patients, in state and federally funded clinical research. No document links this research to the CIA's MKUltra. Source: Wikipedia, Spring Grove Hospital Center.
  • St. Elizabeths Hospital, Washington D.C. blacksite · 1855 · 38.8490, -76.9740St. Elizabeths Hospital, opened 1855 as the Government Hospital for the Insane, the first federally operated psychiatric hospital in the US. Patients included John Hinckley Jr. (1982-2016) and Ezra Pound (1946-1958, found unfit to stand trial for treason). Walter Freeman was its director of laboratories before he developed the transorbital ('ice-pick') lobotomy. The West Campus is now headquarters of the Department of Homeland Security and the Coast Guard. Source: Wikipedia, St. Elizabeths Hospital; Walter Jackson Freeman II.
  • Stasi Headquarters (Normannenstraße), Berlin surveillance · 1990-01-15 · 52.5147, 13.4872Ministry for State Security (MfS) headquarters, Lichtenberg. At its height 91,015 staff and about 174,000 unofficial informants (estimates up to 189,000). Officers shredded files as the GDR collapsed; on 15 January 1990 citizens occupied the building to stop the destruction. About 16,000 bags of shredded paper (roughly 45 million pages) are being reassembled by computer. Source: Wikipedia, Stasi.
  • Sverdlovsk (Yekaterinburg) - Compound 19 Anthrax Leak Site blacksite · 1979-04-02 · 56.8389, 60.6057Compound 19 (Sverdlovsk-19), a Soviet military biological facility. An accidental release of anthrax spores in early April 1979 killed at least 68 people downwind (Meselson et al.). Soviet authorities blamed contaminated meat; Yeltsin was reported in May 1992 to have said 'our military development was the cause', though the post-Soviet government maintains the food explanation. Ken Alibek, former first deputy director of Biopreparat, defected in 1992 and described the Soviet offensive bioweapons programme run in breach of the 1972 Biological Weapons Convention. Pin at city level. Source: Wikipedia, Sverdlovsk anthrax leak; Ken Alibek.
  • Tazmamart Secret Prison, Morocco blacksite · 1972 · 32.2761, -4.3375Secret desert prison in southeastern Morocco, built in 1972 after the 1971 and 1972 coup attempts against King Hassan II. 58 army officers were held in windowless cells for 18 years; 35 died before the prison was closed in 1991 under international pressure. Source: Wikipedia, Tazmamart; ICRC Missing Persons Platform.
  • Tiananmen Square, Beijing - June Fourth Suppression conflict · 1989-06-04 · 39.9054, 116.39764 June 1989: troops cleared Tiananmen Square and surrounding streets. Death toll unknown: estimates range from several hundred (US Ambassador Lilley; an NSA cable, 180-500) to about 1,000 (Amnesty), while a disputed British cable from Ambassador Alan Donald, released 2017, relayed a 'minimum' of 10,000 from a single source. The event remains censored in China; the Tiananmen Mothers group has been suppressed. Source: Wikipedia, 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre.
  • Tuol Sleng (S-21) Prison, Phnom Penh, Cambodia blacksite · 1976 · 11.5495, 104.9176A former high school converted by the Khmer Rouge into Security Prison 21 (S-21), the regime's central interrogation and execution centre; an estimated 20,000 people were held there from 1976 to 1979 and only twelve known survivors are recorded. Now the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum. Source: Wikipedia, Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum; United States Holocaust Memorial Museum.
  • USS Liberty (AGTR-5) attack position, off Sinai military · 1967-06-08 · 31.3830, 33.38308 June 1967 (position approximate). FOIA-SOURCED (NSA reading room, read 18 Aug 2026). The USS Liberty, a US Navy signals-intelligence ship, was attacked by Israeli aircraft and torpedo boats in international waters during the Six-Day War; 34 Americans were killed and about 171 wounded. NSA's declassified collection runs to 17 pages of material - attack reports, situation summaries, operational orders and authorisation memos, an 'Aftermath of Israeli Attack on USS Liberty, 22 June 1967' report, and contemporaneous press coverage from 11 and 17 June. TIER: the attack, the casualties and the documents are documented; whether the attack was deliberate or a misidentification remains disputed between the US and Israeli official accounts and this map does not settle it. Source: NSA Historical Releases - USS Liberty collection.
  • USS Pueblo (AGER-2) seizure position, off Wonsan military · 1968-01-23 · 39.4200, 127.900023 January 1968 (position approximate). FOIA-SOURCED (NSA reading room, read 18 Aug 2026). North Korean forces seized the US signals-intelligence ship USS Pueblo off the east coast of Korea; one crewman was killed and 82 were held for eleven months. NSA released 19 pages of material in July 2021, including 'Lessons Learned' reports comparing the Pueblo and EC-121 incidents, NSA response and action reports, cryptologic-impact assessments, SIGINT reflections covering 23-26 January 1968, and documentation of attempts to recover the material lost with the ship. The Pueblo is still held by North Korea and is moored in Pyongyang as a museum - the only commissioned US Navy vessel in foreign captivity. Source: NSA Historical Releases - USS Pueblo collection.
  • Unit 731 Site, Pingfang District, Harbin, China blacksite · 1936 · 45.6127, 126.6440Imperial Japanese Army biological and chemical warfare unit at Pingfang (facility 1936-1945): vivisection, plague bomb tests, frostbite experiments; over 3,000 prisoners killed in the facility and an estimated 200,000-300,000 deaths from biological warfare in China. The US granted immunity to Shiro Ishii and other key members in exchange for research data; the USSR tried twelve members at Khabarovsk in 1949. The Japanese government has never officially acknowledged the programme, though a Tokyo court recognised it in 2002. Source: Wikipedia, Unit 731.
  • Vacaville - California Medical Facility blacksite · 1960 · 38.3575, -121.9710California Medical Facility, Vacaville - state prison medical facility. In the late 1960s inmates were reportedly given succinylcholine (Anectine), a paralytic that halts breathing while the subject is conscious, as 'aversion therapy'. A CIA role is not established in the sources read. Source: Wikipedia, California Medical Facility; press reports.
  • Villa Grimaldi (Cuartel Terranova), Santiago, Chile blacksite · 1974 · -33.4630, -70.5423A former estate in Peñalolén that Pinochet's secret police (DINA) ran as its most important Santiago torture center from 1974 to 1978; about 4,500 detainees passed through and at least 240 were killed or 'disappeared.' It is now the Parque por la Paz memorial. Source: Wikipedia / Villa Grimaldi Peace Park; Plan Cóndor archive, plancondor.org.
  • Vipeholm Experiments - Lund, Sweden blacksite · 1945 · 55.7045, 13.1915Vipeholm Hospital, Lund (1945-1955): residents with intellectual disabilities were fed large amounts of sticky sweets to provoke tooth decay and study how carbohydrates cause cavities. The study was sponsored by the sugar industry and the dental community, with state involvement; its findings shaped Swedish advice on limiting sweets. Source: Wikipedia, Vipeholm experiments.
  • Willowbrook State School, Staten Island, USA blacksite · 1956 · 40.5965, -74.1509State institution for children with intellectual disabilities (1947-1987). From 1956 to 1971 NYU's Saul Krugman, with Yale's Robert McCollum, deliberately infected resident children with hepatitis to study the disease and gamma globulin; parents' admission of children was reportedly tied to consent. Geraldo Rivera's 1972 exposé brought national infamy; the institution closed in 1987. Source: Wikipedia, Willowbrook State School; C. Elliott, New York Review of Books (Nov. 21, 2024).

Section XVII - 35 locations

  • Antwerp, Belgium - Cocaine Port organized-crime · 51.2194, 4.4025Europe's second-largest port. Massive cocaine transshipment hub, often exceeding Rotterdam in seizure volumes. 'Ndrangheta and Albanian organized crime networks coordinate distribution through the port.
  • Arezzo, Italy - P2 Lodge / Villa Wanda organized-crime · 43.4633, 11.8781Licio Gelli's Villa Wanda - headquarters of Propaganda Due (P2) Masonic lodge. 962 members including 44 parliamentarians, military commanders, intelligence chiefs, financiers, media editors. Gelli's 'Plan of Democratic Rebirth' - a 53-point manifesto for authoritarian capture of Italian democracy through media control, judicial infiltration, and constitutional amendment.
  • Blackfriars Bridge, London - Calvi Murder organized-crime · 1982-06-18 · 51.5106, -0.1036Roberto Calvi - 'God's Banker' - found hanging under Blackfriars Bridge, June 18, 1982. Pockets filled with bricks and cash. First inquest: suicide (1982); second: open verdict (1983); a 2002 forensic report found murder, police reopened it as murder (2003), and a Rome court (2007) found murder but acquitted all five accused.
  • Bologna, Italy - Strategy of Tension organized-crime · 1980-08-02 · 44.5060, 11.3429August 2, 1980: Bologna train station bombing - 85 dead, 200+ wounded. NAR neo-fascists convicted; 2020s Bologna proceedings named P2 head Licio Gelli among the instigators. Vincenzo Vinciguerra (neo-fascist, serving life for the 1972 Peteano bombing) testified that NATO stay-behind networks organized false flag attacks to blame the left and justify authoritarian state responses.
  • Cali - Cali Cartel Stronghold, Colombia organized-crime · 1975 · 3.4108, -76.5812The Cali Cartel, run 1975–1995 by brothers Gilberto and Miguel Rodríguez Orejuela with José Santacruz Londoño and Hélmer Herrera, was headquartered in Cali in the Valle del Cauca and at its peak was cited as controlling some 80% of the cocaine market (estimate). It laundered profits through legitimate fronts such as the Drogas La Rebaja pharmacy chain before its leadership was dismantled in the mid-1990s. Source: InSight Crime (insightcrime.org), 'Gilberto Rodríguez Orejuela, alias The Chess Player'; TIME (time.com), 'The Cali Cartel: New Kings of Coke'.
